019a01e3070944461caeed2352adfdcd7e3c40d8.message:
Closes #34, #35, #36. Part of the audit in #33.

The backend's core safety property is that a construct it cannot lower
fails the compile rather than emitting something plausible. Four places
violated that. Each emitted valid, compiling Rust that was wrong.

1. Constructor `assert` with a non-inlinable call (#34)
   walker.ss emitted `/* TODO */ true`, lowering the assert to
   `assert!(true)` — a precondition that silently never fires.

2. Constructor `if` with a non-inlinable call (#34)
   emit.ss emitted `/* TODO */ true`, making the then-branch
   unconditional and the else-branch dead, so a conditional ledger write
   became unconditional.

3. Catch-all guards in the streaming pass (#35)
   `(guard (c [#t "/* TODO A14 */"]) …)` matched EVERY condition, so a
   deliberate `rust-feature-error` — the very mechanism that guarantees
   unsupported constructs fail — was caught and replaced by a comment
   emitted where an expression belongs. It also converted genuine emitter
   bugs (bad nanopass dispatch, malformed IR) into a comment instead of a
   trace, which is why the next person debugging a wrong constructor
   scaffold would have had no signal.

4. Natives with no Rust binding (#36)
   `keccak256`, `ownPublicKey`, `createZswapInput`, `createZswapOutput`
   carried `(rust "/* TODO */ unimplemented!()")`. Contracts calling them
   compiled cleanly and panicked at run time.

   Fixed structurally rather than by special-casing: the `(rust …)` clause
   is optional and `native-call-site-rust` ALREADY rejects on a #f field,
   so dropping the clause makes absence representable as absence and the
   existing rejection fires. A future unbound native now cannot emit a
   panic by accident — there is no string for it to hide in. The
   explanation for each moves to a comment so the knowledge is kept.

Verified against the built compiler, not assumed:

  keccak256 (--feature-zkir-v3):
    unsupported Compact construct (native-binding-missing): no Rust
    binding for native function __compactRuntime.keccak256

  constructor assert on a non-inlinable circuit:
    probe.compact line 11 char 10: unsupported Compact construct
    (ctor-assert-condition-inline): cannot inline the call to `readFlag`
    used as an `assert` condition in a constructor

Both previously produced compiling output. Diagnostics are located and
name the offending circuit or native.

Honest note on coverage of the `if` case: I could not construct a probe
that reaches it. Every shape tried was handled earlier — the constructor
folds ledger reads against the known initial state, and a witness-valued
condition is rejected by disclosure analysis first. It is the identical
code shape as the assert case and is now guarded, but it may be
unreachable in practice; treat the guard as cheap insurance rather than a
fix for a demonstrated bug.

Byte-parity is unchanged, as predicted: the committed corpus contains zero
`TODO` and zero `unimplemented` across all 68 generated lib.rs, so no
fixture reached any of these paths. They were latent traps for the next
contract shape, not bad output being shipped.

Also adds docs/rust-backend-limitations.md (#39, part 1). It was written on
the ledger-9 line and never existed here — on the branch the CoIP cites as
the reference implementation. Counts verified for THIS branch: 28
rejection sites across 4 passes, 24 distinct kinds. Documents the four
fixed paths as worked examples of the rule, since the rule is easier to
follow with evidence that breaking it is expensive.

Gates: fmt, clippy -D warnings, 48 test groups, byte-parity green and
unchanged, ./compiler/go exit 0 with zero failures.

01b8e44a0d285733cbebca2ed7fba25a217e0f35.message:
Closes did.compact's setVerificationMethod through line 259+ (the
non-native-call rejection from A14). Body progress: line 246
(setVerificationMethod) is now FULLY emitted; next gap surfaces at
setSchnorrJubjubVerificationMethod's Map.insert with struct value
(A16 — `adt-read-with-arg-lowering`).

Two complementary changes:

1. **Hoist impure circuit calls out of assert conds** (mirrors the
   existing witness-hoist pattern). When an `assert(!verificationMethodExists(...), ...)`
   appears in an if-branch:

       let _cr_h0 = self.verification_method_exists(ctx, id.clone())?;
       let ctx = _cr_h0.context;
       compact_assert!(!(_cr_h0.result.clone()), "...");

   New parameter `current-impure-call-binds` (rust-passes-helpers.ss:70)
   parallels `current-witness-call-binds`. New helpers in
   rust-passes-walker.ss:

   - `impure-call-bound`  — alist lookup.
   - `collect-impure-call-subcalls` — walks an Expression for
     `(call <non-pure-user-circuit> args*)` sub-expressions
     (skips witnesses, natives, pure circuits — those have their
     own emission paths).
   - `emit-hoisted-impure-calls` — emits the `let _cr_hN = self.X(ctx, ...)?;`
     + `let ctx = _cr_hN.context;` lines and returns
     (lines, binds) for the caller to feed into
     `current-impure-call-binds`.

   `ctor-call-rust`'s else clause (rust-passes-walker.ss:561) now
   consults `current-impure-call-binds` BEFORE falling to
   `call-rust` (which preserves the existing "non-native-call"
   diagnostic when no hoist is available). On hit, the call
   renders as `<rust-name>.result.clone()`.

   The A12 if-then-else emit clause (rust-passes-streaming.ss)
   in both the per-arm and the final-else assert renderers now:
   collects impure subcalls in the assert cond, emits hoist lines
   inside the branch BEFORE the `compact_assert!`, and
   `parameterize`s `current-impure-call-binds` around the
   `assert-cond-rust` call so the rendering picks up the binds.

2. **Loosen the impure-exported bare-call ctx-expr check**
   (rust-passes-streaming.ss). Previously the streaming walker's
   bare-call handler for impure-exported callees rejected outright
   when `ctx-expr` was not the default `&ctx.current_query_context`.
   That bare-rejection was what caused setVerificationMethod's
   final `recordUpdate()` bare call to fail after the Map.insert
   pl-call (stmt [7]) updated ctx-expr to `&_results_7.context`.

   Now the handler emits a one-line `let ctx = CircuitContext {
   current_query_context: <referent>.clone(), ..ctx };` rebind
   when ctx-expr is non-default, then calls `self.X(ctx, ...)?`
   normally. Symmetric to the A14 post-if-then-else ctx rebind.

07b4da1e98ea896cefa04a3c6f20078495b9d3f3.message:
Carries the identity-key fix to codegen-rust — the branch the CoIP cites
as the reference implementation, and the one where it was still missing.

The vulnerable code is DIFFERENT here, which is why this is not a
cherry-pick. The stdlib `jubjubSchnorrVerify` and `secp256k1EcdsaVerify`
arrived with upstream 0.33 and exist only on the ledger-9 line. On ledger 8
the verifier lives in examples/schnorr_attest_fixture.compact — the neutral
fixture #19 introduced — and carried the same flaw.

With pk = O, ecMul(pk, c) is O for every c, so verification collapses to
`response*G == announcement`: the challenge, and with it the MESSAGE, drops
out. An attacker picks any s, sets response = s and announcement = s*G, and
the pair verifies for EVERY message under that key, with no secret.

Reachable rather than theoretical: `default<JubjubPoint>` IS the identity,
and a ledger cell holds its type's default until written, so a contract
verifying against a key cell that was never set fails OPEN.

Demonstrated, not asserted. The new `identity_public_key_is_rejected`
constructs exactly that forgery against a contract whose attestor-key
witness returns the identity point. Verified it is not vacuous by
temporarily removing the Rust guard and re-running:

  test identity_public_key_is_rejected ... FAILED

i.e. without the guard the forged signature IS accepted. Guard restored and
the diff confirmed clean afterwards.

Two scope limits, stated because they matter more than the fix:

1. The new test exercises the guard in the RUST verifier, not the circuit's.
   The emitter rewrites the generic `schnorrVerify` call into
   `midnight_compact_runtime::schnorr_verify_jubjub`, so the circuit body —
   guard included — never runs on the Rust path. The circuit guard governs
   proving and the TypeScript path and is NOT covered by any test here.

2. That is the #26 divergence, and this change produced the sharpest
   evidence for it I have seen: adding a SECURITY GUARD to the circuit left
   byte-parity COMPLETELY UNCHANGED. The circuit and the Rust path share a
   name and nothing else.

Also corrects the doc comment on the Rust verifier, which claimed its
identity checks matched "the circuit's identity guards". The circuit had
none, and now that it does they still are not exercised together — so the
comment now says what is actually true and points at #26.

Gates: fmt, clippy -D warnings, 48 test groups with byte-parity green and
unchanged, ./compiler/go exit 0 with zero failures and print-rust 10/10.

The underlying flaw is upstream's in origin and was reported privately per
their SECURITY.md; this closes it on the fork's stable line.

0916b2836e5de1b4a9d5757c8c9bb1f2a9c059e7.message:
Replace the hardcoded `dup → idx → popeq` template emitted for every
no-arg `(public-ledger ... read)` IR node with a code path that runs
the adt-op's actual vm-code through `expand-vm-code` — the same
machinery A8 uses for the read-with-arg side (Set.member, HMT.checkRoot,
Map.member/lookup). The template still survives as a last-resort
fallback so adt-ops whose vm-code touches instructions
`vminstr->gather-builder-call` doesn't yet recognise keep compiling.

Before A20, `Set.size()` / `Set.isEmpty()` / `Map.size()` /
`Map.isEmpty()` / `List.isEmpty()` / `List.length()` all lowered to
the template, which reads the *container cell* as the result
AlignedValue and decodes the wrong bytes. After A20 the gather chain
mirrors the real vm-code, e.g.:

  Set.size     → `.dup(0).idx_at_index(N,false).size().popeq(true)`
  Set.isEmpty  → `.dup(0).idx_at_index(N,false).size()
                  .push(false, new_cell(0u64)).eq().popeq(true)`

Changes
-------

compiler/rust-passes-emit.ss
  - `emit-ledger-read-expr` no-arg branch routes through
    `emit-ledger-read-expr-with-args` first (with empty expr*), falling
    back to the template only if expansion fails.
  - `vminstr->gather-builder-call` learns `size` → `.size()` and `type`
    → `.type_()`, the two ops the read-no-arg adt-op vm-code uses on
    top of the already-supported `dup`/`idx`/`push`/`member`/`eq`/`root`/
    `popeq`.
  - `vm-cell-elem->rust` widens `(VMalign N bytes)` lowering beyond
    bytes=1 to also handle bytes=2/4/8 (Set.isEmpty's `(push align-0-8)`
    needs `new_cell(0u64)`).

runtime-rs/src/op_builder.rs
  - `OpProgramGather` learns `.size()` (`Op::Size`) and `.type_()`
    (`Op::Type`), wrapping the upstream variants the codegen now
    targets. No existing builder methods touched.

Verification
------------

  - Cell.read / Counter.read still route through expand-vm-code and
    produce the same gather shape as the old template — covered by the
    existing aliases-fixture / counter / tiny byte-parity snapshots.
  - set_size_fixture.compact (next commit) is a purpose-built byte-parity
    fixture for `Set.isEmpty()` / `Map.isEmpty()` exercising the new
    `.size().push(…0u64…).eq().popeq()` gather chain end-to-end.

* rust-passes: resolve struct-name collisions by fingerprint at all sites

Two same-named structs from distinct module imports (a generic protocol
module instantiated twice, or two modules each exporting `struct Rec`)
must each get a distinct Rust name and use it everywhere. The prior
disambiguation had two latent defects (found in review of the
digital-passport codegen, 218d2c8):

1. The struct fingerprint keyed on (name, field-types) only, so two
   same-named structs whose field types matched but field NAMES differed
   were merged into one Rust struct — the other variant's field accesses
   then hit E0609. Fix: fingerprint on field name + type.

2. The disambiguated name was applied in type positions and the struct
   definition, but value sites emitted the raw name — struct literals,
   `decode_via_field_repr::<T>`, and `T::default()`. A struct renamed
   `Name_1` in its signature was still constructed as `Name` (E0308 /
   E0422). Fix: route all three sites through struct-rust-name.

Root cause of both: names were keyed on eq? node identity and the table
was built from signatures/typedefs/ledger only, so body-site nodes
(distinct IR objects) never resolved. build-struct-rust-name-ht now also
returns a fingerprint->name table; struct-rust-name falls back to it on
an eq? miss, computing the fingerprint with the disambiguation tables
forced empty so the key is stable regardless of live table state. Stdlib
structs (Maybe, MerkleTreePath*, ContractAddress) are excluded so
`Maybe<Fr>` vs `Maybe<bool>` don't fabricate a `Maybe_1`.

Both defects were latent on digital-passport (its colliding structs
differ by type and are never constructed in a body), so this preserves
byte-parity: all 28 existing codegen_regression fixtures regenerate
byte-identically. New struct_collision_fixture reproduces both — it
fails to compile against the pre-fix compiler and passes after. See
docs/adr/0001-rust-struct-name-disambiguation.md.

* rust-passes: walker — interleaved bare-call in if-branch (did 0.5.0)

did.compact 0.5.0's controller-authorization model interleaves a
non-terminal compatibility-assert circuit call between an if-branch's
guard assert and its terminal mutating op:

  if (mutation == MapMutation.Update) {
    assert(verificationMethods.member(id), "...");            // guard
    assertExistingVerificationMethodRelationsCompatible(id, crv);  // <- non-terminal bare call
    verificationMethods.remove(id);                           // terminal op
  }

exactly one terminal (pl-call or A17 bare-call), so both
setVerificationMethod and setVerificationMethodRelation fell through to
`no walker shape matched circuit body`.

(walker.ss) that captures non-terminal bare calls, and emit each in the
streaming A12 arm/else emitters (streaming.ss) as
`self.<helper>(ctx.clone(), ...)?` + gas, after the guard assert and
before the terminal op. These compat asserts only read the ledger (no
mutation), so ctx.clone() is safe and no context rebind is needed.

now generates the ENTIRE did.compact 0.5.0 contract (EXIT 0, 5216 lines).

non-terminal branch bare-call, which no existing fixture has). The
generated Rust still has ~15 downstream compile gaps (Schnorr native-call
context construction, ctx move-vs-borrow in ledger-read args,
constructor-context helper calls) tracked as the next codegen step.

* walker: thread zswap-local state through ctor-mode impure calls (A25)

impure-call lowering (A22) always seeded the callee with
`ctx.empty_zswap_local_state.clone()` and only re-extracted the query

subsequent call from the empty state.

- impure-call-thread-lines now seeds the first ctor impure call from
  `ctx.empty_zswap_local_state`, chains subsequent calls off `_zswap`,

- The ConstructorResult emitters read `ctor-zswap-result-field`, which
  returns the threaded `_zswap` when present, else `ctx.empty_zswap_local_state`.

non-terminal call would silently lose its effects and the terminal op
would run against stale ctx.

source position) and drive them through the ordered emitter:
- `emit-branch-body-items` now emits asserts / binds / calls in source

  (via `current-qctx-ref`) and returning `(final-qctx . final-owned)`.
- The pl-call terminal runs against `final-qctx`; the bare-call (A17)
  terminal consumes `final-owned` (moving the last call's context)
  instead of cloning the original ctx.
- Gated on `(or multi-assert has-call)`, so call-free / single-assert
  branches keep their existing emit path.

changelog, flake.nix, compiler-version.ss, and ledger-adt.mdx all agree on
0.31.106.


* codegen: accumulate impure-callee gas in circuit bodies (A27)

Codex review of the did.compact 0.5.0 circuits found gas under-reporting:
a circuit calling an impure helper (recordUpdate() after a mutation, a
cross-circuit call, or the rotate/recover assert helpers) rebound `ctx`
from the callee but dropped the callee's `gas_cost`, so the function
returned only the terminal write's gas.

- Streaming walker: emit `__gas_acc += _cr.gas_cost` after bare/const
  impure calls (setVerificationMethod's recordUpdate, cross-circuit const
  calls).
- Non-streamed circuit bodies: when the body has an impure call
  (`body-has-impure-circuit-call?`), seed a `__gas_acc`, accumulate each
  callee's gas via impure-call-thread-lines, and return
  `__gas_acc + results.gas_cost`. Fixes rotateControllerKey /
  recoverControllerKey. Gated by `circuit-gas-acc?` (defaults #f), so
  bodies without impure calls are byte-identical.

Also corrects the latent same-shape gap in cross-circuit-fixture. New
semantic test asserts `reset_and_set` gas strictly exceeds `reset` gas
(it does reset()'s work plus a write); did-05 + cross-circuit fixtures
lock the corrected output. Version bumped 0.31.106 -> 0.31.107.


* walker: constructor read-your-writes before impure calls (A28)

Codex review (P1): the did.compact 0.5.0 constructor writes controllerPublicKey
/ recoveryAuthorityPublicKey from witnesses, then calls
assertControllerPublicKeyDistinctFromRecoveryAuthority(controllerPublicKey),
which reads BOTH keys from the ledger. The codegen batched every write into a
single OpProgramVerify applied at the end, so the assert's argument read AND
the callee's internal recoveryAuthority read ran against the unmodified initial
ledger, comparing JubjubPoint::default() values — silently defeating the
distinctness security invariant.

Flush the pending writes before the impure call so reads see the written
fields (read-your-writes):
- Extract `cell-write-op-lines` (per-write builder lines) from emit-body-writes.
- `ctor-write-flush-lines`: emit the pending tagged mutations (cell-write +
  pl-call) as an OpProgramVerify, apply via query_for_verify(&qctx, ...), and
  rebind `qctx` to the result.
- Both ctor impure-call sites emit the flush before the call and reset the
  pending-writes accumulator; the impure call's args and the callee then read
  the flushed qctx. The remaining post-call writes (created/updated) flush at
  the end as before.

did.compact's constructor now flushes the 6 leading writes, so _carg_6_0 and
the assert helper read the witnessed controller/recovery keys. Gated to
constructors with an impure call, so other constructors are byte-identical.
Covered by a structural regression test (flush must precede the distinctness
assert) + the did-05 byte-parity/compile gates. Version 0.31.107 -> 0.31.108.

0da200a77b48dab83223639772ad7218fae83ce9.message:
Three borrow-checker fixes for did.compact's generated lib.rs body
shapes. All tests-e2e-rust byte-parity fixtures (28 test groups)
continue to pass.

Bug-5 — duplicate `let tmp = X` in arm pre-stmts
  The frontend lift can emit the same `(= tmp expr)` more than once
  per arm when the same elt-ref / arg expression is referenced from
  both the arm's assert cond and its terminal pl-call. Rust then
  rejects the second `let tmp = ...` with E0382. Dedupe by rendered
  Rust name when iterating pre-stmts in the A12 if-arm emit; the
  second occurrence is structurally identical (same lift, same expr)
  so skipping it preserves semantics.

Bug-6 — non-Copy var-ref / elt-ref lifted to a `let` without clone
  Three sites in the body walker emitted `let tmp = X.id;` where
  `X.id` is non-Copy. The bare assignment partial-moves `X.id` (and
  the parent X), breaking later borrows. Route each lifted RHS
  through `expr-rust-arg-cloned` so a `.clone()` suffix lands when
  the expression is a non-Copy var-ref or rooted elt-ref:
    * arm pre-stmts emit  (rust-passes-streaming.ss arm-info loop)
    * top-level const-binding else-branch
      (rust-passes-streaming.ss emit-streaming-body)
    * emit-body-or-fallback const-binding clause
      (rust-passes-walker.ss)
  Literal-coerced RHSs (Uint<N> integer literals etc.) are emitted
  unchanged — they're already Copy at the Rust layer.

Bug-7 — `ctx` moved into a hoisted impure call inside an if-arm
  emit-hoisted-impure-calls (rust-passes-walker.ss) emitted
  `self.X(ctx, ...)` consuming ctx, but when the hoist runs inside
  an arm of an if-chain the outer scope still needs ctx for the
  post-arm `CircuitContext { ..ctx }` rebind. Detect arm context by
  indent depth (> 8 spaces) and emit `ctx.clone()` there. The
  top-level body keeps the existing move semantics (no behaviour
  change for current fixtures).

Net effect: did.compact's generated lib.rs error count drops from
37 → 25 unique compile errors. All remaining errors are
EmbeddedGroupAffine / [Fr; 4] trait impls (orphan-rule blocked at
the runtime layer) plus one Schnorr module-import resolution issue.

0fffe67029f1ddccde31f2f9a7aa5b852e5074af.message:
Bug-4 (commit c58d563) added `(tenum-name-of-type type)` as the first
check in the `==` / `!=` typed-enum heuristic. The intent was to handle
did.compact's `disclosed_mutation == MapMutation.Insert` where neither
operand-side heuristic fires (disclose isn't a witness/circuit, the
var-ref isn't a formal arg) but the IR carries `type = MapMutation`.

The misfire: the `==` IR node's `type` is the declared Compact tenum
even when one operand is a ledger-read whose Rust decoder produces
u8. Election's `state.read() == PublicState.commit` regressed —
`state` is `Cell<PublicState>`, so the IR `==` type is `PublicState`,
Bug-4's first check fires, both sides render typed →
`u8 == PublicState::commit`, which doesn't compile.

The walker comment at rust-passes-walker.ss:181-191 already documented
the intended split: "The default integer rendering still covers
tiny.compact's `state == STATE.unset` (LHS is a u8-decoded ledger
read) and election's `state.read() == PublicState.commit` (same:
ledger decoder produces u8)." Bug-4 violated its own design.

Fix: short-circuit `typed?` to #f when either operand is a
`public-ledger` IR node (stripping casts). Bug-4's case still emits
typed enums because `disclose(mutation)` is not a ledger-read —
verified by regenerating did.compact's contract: all 18 sites still
emit `MapMutation::Insert` / `SetMutation::Insert` etc.

Same fix applies symmetrically to the `!=` clause.

New helper `is-ledger-read-expr?` lives next to `operand-typed-enum?`
in the helpers block above ctor-expr-rust.

10dd2242ae29aa4d6543df0337a0bc2986501779.message:
## Problem

Nix-based builds of `compactc` (and everything depending on it) fail
while fetching crate tarballs:

```
curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 403
error: cannot download crate-actix-http-3.11.2.tar.gz from any mirror
error: Cannot build '/nix/store/...-cargo-vendor-dir.drv'.
       Reason: 1 dependency failed.
```

This is not a code regression: the pinned nixpkgs (`bcc4a9d`,
2026-02-18) fetches each crate tarball from the
`https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/<crate>/<version>/download` endpoint
with the plain `curl/*` User-Agent that older nixpkgs fetchers use, and
crates.io's CDN now returns **403** to that User-Agent (reproducible
with any crate; see rust-lang/crates.io#13482). `static.crates.io`
serves the same files with any User-Agent.

The same problem was diagnosed and fixed in
`hyperledger-identus/neoprism` by nixpkgs update: see
hyperledger-identus/neoprism#313.

## Fix

1. Update the pinned nixpkgs to `c27cdad` (2026-08-27, nixpkgs-unstable)
— root input plus the nested `nixpkgs` inputs of the
midnight-ledger-based inputs (`zkir`, `zkir-wasm`, `zkir-v3`,
`zkir-v3-wasm`, `onchain-runtime-v3`), which also fetch crates. Newer
nixpkgs Rust fetchers download from `static.crates.io` with a
`nixpkgs-fetchCargoVendor/2` User-Agent, which is not affected by the
new CDN policy.

2. Compatibility fixes required by the newer nixpkgs (all three of these
toolsets were removed from nixpkgs after the pinned rev):

- `pkgs.nodePackages.typescript` → `pkgs.typescript` (`nodePackages`
removed 2026-03-24; `typescript` is available at the top level).
- `pkgs.mkYarnModules` → `fetchYarnDeps` + `yarnConfigHook` (yarn2nix
tooling removed 2026-04-25) for `compact-vscode-extension-node-modules`.
`nodejs` is added to `nativeBuildInputs` so that `patchShebangs`
(invoked by `yarnConfigHook`) can rewrite the `#!/usr/bin/env node`
shebangs, which would otherwise break inside the build sandbox where
`/usr/bin/env` does not exist.

## Verification (x86_64-linux)

- ✅ `nix build .` (`compact-all`)
- ✅ `nix build .#compactc`
- ✅ `nix build .#compactc-binary`
- ✅ `nix build .#compact-vscode-extension` (all 23 tests pass, `.vsix`
packaged)
- ✅ `nix build .#runtime.forPublish`

    `compactc --rust`. Diffs are limited to:

      * `#[derive(.., Default)]` + `#[default]` on enums that have them.

1a8778d5d433db9dd51121fe30bf928989de4796.message:
Generalises the walker in three small, non-regressive steps that are
prerequisites for handling did.compact's helper-call pattern.

1. rust-passes.ss — drop the `id-exported?` gate on the impure-circuit
   emission filter. Non-exported impure circuits (private helpers like
   did.compact's `recordUpdate`, `assertController`,
   `assertControllerCanUpdate`) now emit as `pub(crate) fn` methods on
   the Contract impl, provided their bodies match one of the supported
   walker shapes. A new pre-flight predicate
   `impure-circuit-body-walkable?` mirrors emit-impure-circuit's body
   dispatch so non-walkable helpers (e.g. tiny.compact's `in_state` —
   non-unit single return-expression, not yet a supported shape) stay
   filtered out exactly as before, preserving 144+ tests-e2e-rust
   parity.

2. rust-passes-emit.ss — emit-impure-circuit now uses `pub` for
   exported impure circuits and `pub(crate)` for non-exported ones,
   mirroring emit-pure-circuit's visibility convention.

3. rust-passes-walker.ss —
   - classify-call: drop the `id-exported?` requirement on the impure
     branch. Both exported and non-exported impure circuit calls now
     classify as 'impure-exported (kept tag for emission-clause
     simplicity); the emit shapes are identical so downstream code
     paths need no change.
   - body-walkable?: drop the non-terminal restriction on bare-call
     statements. The emit-body-or-fallback loop's bare-call clause
     already handles terminal positions correctly — the accumulated
     writes from earlier statements anchor the OpProgramVerify chain,
     and a body with no writes naturally falls through to #f at the
     (null? stmts) tail.

did.compact still fails to emit `rotateControllerKey` because its
helper `recordUpdate`'s own body — two non-write public-ledger calls
followed by a Cell write — isn't yet a supported walker shape. Tracked
as gap A4 in ADR 0006. Closing A4 is the next concrete step before
midnight-did-runtime can regenerate.

1c66b3281c0cafabe179f9f8244a50d2a87b1595.message:
Closes two compiler-side bugs surfaced by did.compact's generated lib.rs
in the post-A19 inventory.

Bug-1 — `id` not in scope inside inlined ADT-read calls.
- inline-circuit-call binds formal→rendered-actual via local-binds for
  ctor-expr-rust's var-ref clause, but expressions reaching expr-rust
  (via emit-ledger-read-expr → expr->vm-value → expr-rust) lose
  local-binds at the boundary, so the inner formal id leaked into the
  final Rust as `new_cell(id.clone())` instead of
  `new_cell(disclosed_method_id.clone())`.
- Fix: new dynamic parameter `current-var-substitution` mirrors
  ctor-expr-rust's local-binds for the duration of one render.
  ctor-expr-rust parameterizes it at entry; expr-rust's var-ref clause
  consults it before falling back to plain snake-case. Two sites in
  did.compact's setVerificationMethodRelation now compile cleanly.

Bug-3 — CircuitContext::clone trait bound not satisfied.
- A17 introduced `ctx.clone()` for the drifted-ctx CircuitContext
  splicing shape (helper-call after asserts). CircuitContext<PS>
  derives Clone iff PS: Clone, and the generated `impl<PS, W>
  Contract<PS, W>` block lacked the bound.
- Fix: add `PS: Clone` to the where-clause in emit-contract-struct.
  Upward-compatible — consumers that don't use Clone aren't affected.

Net effect: did.compact's generated lib.rs error count drops from
60 → 56 unique compile errors. All tests-e2e-rust byte-parity
fixtures pass (28 test groups, all green). Remaining errors are
Bug-2 (ConstructorContext drift), R5 (runtime trait impls), and a
suspected midnight-did-rs Cargo pin lag.

25fba53c6e3b342c4439221ee31f3d3e8cc1078f.message:
Cross-language byte-parity test crate that validates `compactc --rust`
output against the existing TypeScript backend. For every `.compact`
example under examples/, there's:

  - examples/<name>.compact                                 — Compact source
  - tests-e2e-rust/contracts/<name>-fixture/                — Rust crate generated by compactc --rust
  - tests-e2e-rust/fixtures/<name>-ts-state.json            — captured TS reference state
  - tests-e2e-rust/fixtures/capture-<name>.mjs              — capture driver
  - tests-e2e-rust/tests/<name>_fixture.rs                  — Rust byte-parity test

Each test drives the Rust contract through initial_state() (plus any
multi-step impure circuit sequence the fixture's TS driver exercises),
serializes the resulting ContractState via midnight_serialize::
tagged_serialize, and asserts byte equality with the TS capture.

Fixture matrix:
- counter, tiny — single-contract anchors; tiny is the multi-step
  byte-parity workhorse (init → clear → set(99) → get).
- list-fixture, set-fixture, map-fixture, nested-map-fixture — ADTs.
- for-range-fixture, for-iter-fixture, fold-fixture,
  map-fn-fixture, map-lambda-fixture — control flow + map() with
  literal-iterable bodies (and non-identity lambdas via wrapping_*).
- uints-fixture, vector-fixture, bounded-uint-fixture — primitive
  type coverage.
- aliases-fixture — transparent + nominal type aliases.
- witnesses-fixture — witness threading + a negative witness-leak
  regression test asserting that private state never appears in the
  serialised ContractState bytes.
- if-stmt-fixture — if-then-else body shape (pure circuit branch).
- cross-circuit-fixture — impure circuit calling impure circuit.
- module-fixture — module / import (closed by frontend desugaring).
- sealed-ledger-fixture — sealed `Field` / `Bytes<32>` / `Uint<64>`
  fields with literal RHS in the constructor.
- pure-circuit-fixture — standalone `pure circuit` modifier coverage.
- hash-to-curve-fixture — hashToCurve byte-parity.
- zerocash — full multi-step (init → mint → spend) byte-parity with
  MerkleTreePath replay from the TS driver.
- election — full multi-step (init → set_topic → advance → add_voter
  → vote$commit → vote$reveal) with explicit constructor + path
  replay for the eligibility and committed-votes Merkle trees.

Test infrastructure:
- tests-e2e-rust/src/ split into per-contract reference-state shapes
  (common.rs, tiny.rs, zerocash.rs, election.rs, map_fixture.rs) so
  a fixture author can find the shape relevant to their contract
  without skimming unrelated ones.
- tests-e2e-rust/tests/codegen_regression.rs — re-runs `compactc
  --rust` against every example and asserts the emitted lib.rs is
  byte-identical to the committed one. Catches the failure mode
  where the codegen produces broken Scheme that the build hides
  because the test suite drives the *committed* lib.rs, not freshly-
  regenerated output.
- tests-e2e-rust/README.md — fixture-authoring recipe + failure-mode
  troubleshooting.

~40 e2e tests across byte-parity, codegen-regression guard, and
per-fixture direct-invocation tests. Together with the 44 compact-
runtime unit tests, the suite totals 85+ passing locally.

examples/election.compact carries an explicit constructor needed to
unblock the multi-step byte-parity tests — public_key(sk) == authority
would otherwise fail with the implicit zero authority.

2e4da399d1c59c440d9c8593fef1e037a106492a.message:
Closes #37. Part of the audit in #33.

The backend is ~10k lines across 9 files, and 8 of the 9 had no
file-level comment at all — they went straight from the licence block
into a helper definition. Every file now states what it owns, what calls
into it, and what it must not do.

CORRECTION to the audit's finding B1, worth stating plainly because it
changed the shape of this commit: the repo was NOT without a module map.
`compiler/README-rust-passes.md` already existed and is good — pipeline
position, a per-file table with "touch when..." guidance, and the genuinely
useful tip that reading typescript-passes.ss is often the fastest way to
learn what an IR node should produce. I missed it because I only looked in
doc/ and docs/.

So this does not add a second map. I wrote one, found the existing one, and
folded the new material into it instead — two maps would diverge, and the
right place for this is next to the code where a compiler engineer looks.

What the README gained:
  - the walker/emit split, and its cost: both layers must understand the
    same IR shapes, so a new construct usually needs handling in BOTH.
    Emitter-without-walker is silently unsupported; walker-without-emitter
    is a crash.
  - the three body routes (constructor / impure / pure) and why they differ
  - what each test layer can and cannot catch. Byte-parity locks the TEXT,
    executing tests lock the MEANING: a wrong lowering that happens to
    serialise identically passes byte-parity, and a correct lowering that
    is merely reformatted fails it.

What it had wrong. Its Conventions section said walkers should "bail to
`unimplemented!()` rather than producing wrong code". That is the same
mistake in a different costume — it defers failure to run time instead of
preventing it — and it is exactly what f3a98aa removed in four places. The
convention now states the rejection contract and points at the four worked
examples.

Also stale and now fixed: "seven Scheme files" (nine), every LOC figure,
and a missing table row for rust-passes-naming.ss.

Dangling pointers into docs/superpowers/** removed from everything that
ships. That directory is a dated internal journal that will not exist
upstream, so `rust-passes.ss`'s only orientation pointer led nowhere — and
three links in runtime-rs / runtime-rs-macros would have shipped as broken
links in published rustdoc. Where a pointer was load-bearing the fact is
now stated inline (e.g. the `=` version pin is what enforces the
runtime/macros lockstep, not a plan document).

Comment- and doc-only: verified no non-comment line changed in any .ss
file. Byte-parity green and unchanged, ./compiler/go exit 0 with zero
failures, fmt and clippy clean.

350a09a3711fb2af361a1f7230203eacf22387c2.message:
A20 worker (2026-06-26) flagged a "bounded-Uint write alignment gap"
when scoping the set_size_fixture. Phase F.2 investigation confirmed
that gap does NOT reproduce at HEAD c6c73c0 — Uint<8> writes from u64
sources work byte-parity clean.

The investigation surfaced a distinct gap instead: Uint<L..U> bounded
ranges with non-power-of-2 upper bounds (e.g. Uint<0..100>,
Uint<0..70000>) reject in the walker when RHS is non-literal. Root
cause: tunsigned-rust-suffix-for-bound (rust-passes-walker.ss:464-471)
only accepts the standard nat ladder {255, 65535, 4294967295,
u64::MAX, u128::MAX}; other values fall through to #f, body walker
bails with "no walker shape matched".

Fix is multi-file (~80-150 LOC):
- generalise tunsigned-rust-suffix-for-bound to arbitrary nat≤u128::MAX
- cell-builder selection: non-power-of-2 byte widths need
  new_cell_bounded_uint(tmp as u128, byte_len), not new_cell::<T>
- verify decode_uN round-trips for byte_len < Rust width

Filing as latent backlog item (post-A21 walker gap). Conservative
gate stays as-is — it correctly catches shapes that would miscompile.
Workaround for A20-style size-write coverage: use the existing
working Uint<8> form, which is already exercised by set_size_fixture.

Finding doc:
docs/superpowers/notes/2026-06-26-bounded-uint-write-alignment.md

3b9217e8578f239d62bee09fc12740b19ef8352b.message:
## Why

PR #705's Compiler Build failed after roughly 2h24m because a stale
generated Rust fixture was found inside a late native gate. The compiler
producer was already an authenticated, SHA-bound same-run closure; the
long serial consumer was the bottleneck. This PR implements the graph in
#708 on `codex/rust-backend-ast` and consolidates measurement drafts
#709–#715.

## Graph and ownership

## Measured evidence

- Baseline neighboring successful gate: about 154 minutes. The failed PR
#705 run stopped at about 143 minutes, finding its stale fixture after a
42-minute native step.
- Complete hosted gates: #713 77m34s wall / 178.95 runner-min; #714
72m54s / 199.10 runner-min; #715 64m53s / 270.47 runner-min; first #716
68m59s / 314.55 runner-min; second #716 61m22s / 308.78 runner-min;
final split #716 attempt 1 56m49s / 346.78 runner-min and same-head full
attempt 4 57m16s / 360.35 runner-min. All strict aggregators passed.
Hosted #715 logs confirm all 26 native selectors passed exactly once.
Different SHAs and overlapping load make these indicative comparisons,
not controlled speedups.
- First #716's remaining Rust proof owner took 51m01s, with four serial
product checks consuming its final 17m42s. Its API owner's workspace
Cargo test took 16m18s after other checks. The workspace/product split
moved those measured tails to independent owners. The second gate passed
but missed the under-60-minute milestone by 1m22s because the combined
product owner ran 40m10s after fixtures. The latest follow-up isolates
its final 6m54s component Vector proof in another owner with an explicit
aggregate dependency. Its first exact-head complete gate passed under 60
minutes; the native wallet/core owner was the new critical path at
36m33s after fixtures. The extra lane increased summed runner use by
38.00 minutes versus the prior #716 run.
- Local validation after the follow-up: 459 backend tests run, 20
expected skips, zero failures after a stale test expectation was
corrected; 21 compiler closure/workflow tests pass; YAML parses as 18
jobs; Bash syntax and diff checks pass. Original qualification commands
and success diagnostics retain an owner.

## Hosted acceptance

The latest component Vector split passed every owner and the strict
aggregate twice at the exact `93f7a3c2c` head: [attempt
1](https://github.com/betsudo/compact/actions/runs/42164920928/attempts/1)
in 56m49s and [full attempt
4](https://github.com/betsudo/compact/actions/runs/42164920928/attempts/4)
in 57m16s. Downloaded attempt-1 logs match all 26 exact native selectors
to the checked-in manifest once each (8/10/8). Attempt 2 hit a GitHub
runner disk-full crash during component Vector Nix verification before
proof execution; all other qualification owners passed and the aggregate
correctly failed. Targeted attempt 3 passed that full proof owner and
aggregate. Both full green attempts restored the same warm ~110 MB Cargo
cache. A controlled cold/warm same-head delta is not available; the
earlier cold-cache slices used different SHAs. The 20–30-minute target
remains a stretch, and repeated Nix/proof setup plus native wallet/core
are the measured limits. The 20–30 minute target is a stretch given
observed producer (12–15m), full fixtures (5–6m), repeated Nix setup and
proof/native work. The first milestone is a complete gate under 60
minutes with earlier stale-fixture feedback.

Closes #708 after hosted acceptance and review.

3e0c70aac008c8df8a87165f1d76c38741141f85.message:
f90c344 turned the byte-parity test's missing-compiler path from a silent
SKIP into a hard failure, but did not update its only CI caller. The
`Test ubuntu-latest` / `Test macos-*` jobs in rust-runtime-test.yml are
bare runners with no `nix build`, so they went red on every PR.

The hard failure is correct and stays: a skip there reported a green
byte-parity gate that regenerated nothing, which is what it had been
doing for the entire life of the branch. Rather than restore an in-test
escape hatch, the bare-runner job now excludes that single test by name.
The distinction matters — the test keeps no skip path of its own, so any
run that executes it is guaranteed to have had a real compiler, and the
exclusion is visible in the workflow step and in libtest's "filtered out"
count instead of hidden inside the test.

Everything else in tests-e2e-rust still gates on these runners;
codegen_regression.rs holds only this one test.

Filed #23 to make the gate genuinely run in CI by sharing the compactc
that build-compiler.yml already builds. Until then it is enforced
locally, which is where our test loop lives.

4691d3f6d32cf0b9813da4293590cfc5b8b7f72f.message:
Generalises the body walker's public-ledger handling so multi-index
write paths are admitted and emitted via the existing
expand-vm-code + vminstr->builder-call pipeline, instead of being
rejected by the single-index gate at body validation time.

Before: stmt->public-ledger-write required `(fx= (length path-elt*) 1)`,
which forced the body-walkable? / body-streaming-walkable? predicates
to reject any write whose ledger field lives at a nested path (e.g.
a Cell field under a sub-ledger struct). The hardcoded
push(idx)/push(val)/ins(1) template in emit-body-writes only
handles depth-1 cells, so the predicates were correctly conservative
about not admitting them.

After: a new predicate `single-index-cell-write?` (rust-passes-walker.ss:2166)
identifies exactly the legacy single-index shape. The non-terminal
and terminal pl-call clauses in `body-walkable?` and the pl-call
clause in `body-streaming-walkable?` drop their length=1 gate and
instead require every path element to be a path-index (numeric);
multi-index writes now flow through the pl-call mutation tag in
emit-body-mutations, which lowers each write via expand-vm-code
+ vminstr->builder-call (the same path Counter.increment etc.
already use).

The emit-body-or-fallback dispatch site at rust-passes-walker.ss:2080
swaps `stmt->public-ledger-write` for `single-index-cell-write?` in
its negation so multi-index writes get the pl-call tag (vm-code path)
rather than falling through to the legacy cell-write tag.

Non-regressive: 24 tests-e2e-rust codegen_regression fixtures still
pass — none of them have nested-ledger writes, so the relaxed
predicates behave identically for single-index writes (the legacy
push/push/ins template still wins via single-index-cell-write?).

Scope note: this is the walker / dispatch half of the multi-index
Cell.write story. The vm-code that `write` adt-ops carry for nested
paths is generated by an earlier compiler pass (independent of these
walker changes) and the existing path-elt->vm-value + expand-vm-code
already accept arbitrary path-index lists. did.compact's
rotateControllerKey is the motivating case (controllerPublicKey lives
at path (0 1)), but its compilation is still blocked by an earlier
walker gap (recordUpdate body — disclose() + assignment-statement
lowering), tracked separately.
4691d3f6d32cf0b9813da4293590cfc5b8b7f72f.subject: rust-passes: A10 — route multi-index Cell.write through vm-code emission

470b234cd108f32627f9e5170cd9b8b7f87b6322.message:
Investigation outcome: PRIORITY (real divergence, not a parallel
limitation).

- Empirical usage: 39/301 bounded-range occurrences in compactc's
  upstream test corpus use non-power-of-2 upper bounds across
  14 .compact test files. Zero usage in production contracts
  (did.compact, ledger, zswap).
- Language spec: explicitly sanctions Uint<m..n> with arbitrary
  bounds — documented feature, not a corner case.
- TS backend: `CompactTypeUnsignedInteger` handles arbitrary byte
  widths via its parametric `length` field. Zero limitation TS-side.
- Rust backend: walker's `tunsigned-rust-suffix-for-bound` gate
  unilaterally rejects non-{255, 65535, 4294967295, u64::MAX,
  u128::MAX} upper bounds for non-literal writes.

Practical implication: any real Compact contract using
`Uint<0..n>` for non-power-of-2 `n` plus non-literal circuit
assignments would compile under TS but fail under `compactc --rust`.
A documented spec divergence.

No current consumer is blocked today — but the gap should be closed
before a real consumer surfaces. The ~80-150 LOC fix is filed at
`docs/superpowers/notes/2026-06-26-bounded-uint-write-alignment.md`
(commit 350a09a). This survey doc records the impact assessment that
justifies promoting Bug-11 from "latent backlog item" to "real fix
worth scheduling".
470b234cd108f32627f9e5170cd9b8b7f87b6322.subject: docs: file Bug-11 reality check — Uint<L..U> non-power-of-2 IS a real gap

4f743ecca8542ebfdf5a7598baff7cc7aaa5c6dc.message:
Fixes #90, #91 and #21, and the call-argument case of #83.

This PR ships two fixes for the same class of bug: a call argument
reaching the Rust emitter with no expected type.
- **Part 1 (#90, 0.31.121):** a stopgap for Field-only literals.
- **Part 2 (#91, 0.31.122):** the general fix. Every call argument now
renders at the callee's declared formal type.

## ⚠️ Silent wrong hash: `persistentCommit`

`persistentCommit<Field>(0 as Field, o)` was emitted as
`persistent_commit(&0, …)`. It **built**: `persistent_commit` is generic
over `T: BinaryHashRepr`, which every Rust integer implements, so Rust
inferred `i32` and committed to its 4 little-endian bytes instead of the
`Fr` encoding. The commitment differed from the TS target's, with no
build or runtime signal. It now emits `&Fr::from(0u64)`. The new parity
test fails on the pre-fix emitter at `commitSmall`. The existing
`persistentCommit` parity (the dogfood contract) passes only typed
locals, whose Rust type is fixed, so it could not see this.

## Part 2: call arguments at the declared formal type (#91)

### Problem

The typechecker wraps a call argument in `safe-cast` only when its type
differs from the formal's (`maybe-safecast`). The emitter took a call
argument's expected type from that wrapper alone, so an argument whose
type already was the formal rendered with no expected type:
- `[0 as Field, 1 as Field]` into a `Vector<2, Field>` parameter emitted
`[0, 1]` for pure circuits, witnesses and impure circuits (#21), and
`AlignedValue::from(0)` in `persistentHash` / `transientHash`. None of
these built.
- `persistentCommit` built with the wrong value (above).

### Fix

- **Formal-type table:** `current-callee-formal-types` maps id →
declared formal types for natives, witnesses and circuits. Declarations
are monomorphised, so generic natives get their instantiated types. The
table is bound at the top of the Rust pass.
- **One entry point:** `call-args-rust` renders each argument at `(or
<safe-cast target> <formal>)`. A wrapped argument therefore renders
exactly as before. It has an `expr-rust` form and a walker form; both
apply the shared clone decision, and the walker form also does the enum
ledger-read decode.
- **Call sites switched:** `call-rust` (`some`/`none`, 1:1 natives, pure
circuits), `ctor-call-rust`, the flat-body and streaming walkers
(`const`/bare witness, pure and impure calls, hoisted calls, A17/A26).
- **Special cases:** `persistentCommit` renders its value and opening at
their formals. `persistentHash`/`transientHash` use the formal as the
atom target for an unwrapped argument. `inline-circuit-call` renders
each actual at its formal, with no clone added.
- **Tuple/vector bridge:** the #83 bridge now applies at call arguments.
- **Removed:** `pure-call-arg-rust`, `render-pure-circuit-arg` and
`circuit-formal-arg-types`, which had no callers left.
- **Guard:** `tests/call_args_guard.rs` fails if `arg-rust-clone-if-var`
/ `pure-call-arg-rust` is called outside `call-args-rust`. Its allowlist
of ledger ADT argument and cell-write users names each function and how
many direct calls it may contain, so a new direct call inside
`emit-streaming-body`, which also holds call sites, still fails. The
failure names the file, function and lines. I checked it by reverting
one site.

### Tests

- New fixture `call_arg_declared_type_fixture`, tested by
`tests/call_arg_declared_type.rs`. It has 16 exported circuits, each
writing its result to the ledger, and the test compares the state bytes
after each one against the TS capture. Coverage:
- `persistentCommit<Field>` of `N as Field` for small, `u128`-range and
above-`max-unsigned` `N`;
- the #21 vector into a pure circuit from a pure body and from an impure
body, into a witness (`const` and bare), and into an impure circuit
(`const`, bare, and bare in an `if` arm);
- the vector into an impure circuit inlined into an `assert` condition,
and into a conditional-expression condition (constructor);
  - the vector into `persistentHash` / `transientHash`;
  - the #90 literal as a pure-circuit argument;
  - tuple → `Vector` and `Vector` → tuple parameters.
- `codegen_regression`: every other committed fixture is byte-identical.
- #90 fallback check: with the `(> datum (max-unsigned))` branch
temporarily removed, the whole corpus regenerated byte-identically,
including `literal-coercion-fixture` and the new fixture. The branch is
kept as a backstop.

- `nix build .#compactc` ✅
- `./compiler/go` ✅
- `cargo fmt --check` ✅
- `cargo clippy -D warnings` ✅
- `cargo test -p midnight-compact-runtime -p tests-e2e-rust` ✅ (59

### Known gaps (not in this PR)

- The backend does not lower an impure call used as an `if`
*statement's* condition, even with a scalar argument; this predates the
PR. Condition inlining is covered through a conditional expression and
an `assert` instead.
- Ledger ADT operation arguments are unchanged by this PR:
- `Set<Vector<2, Field>>.member([0 as Field, 1 as Field])` renders the
key as `[0, 1]`, which builds as `[u8; 2]`, so the membership check
silently looks up the wrong value.
  - A vector-keyed `Set`/`Map` `insert` does not build.

  Follow-up: #93.

## Part 1: Field-only literals in call arguments (#90)

### Problem

An `N as Field` literal above `max-unsigned` (2^248 - 1) passed as a
call argument (stdlib native or user pure circuit) was emitted as bare
digits. `compactc` exited 0, then `cargo build` failed with `integer
literal is too large`. This blocked Rust codegen for
`@midnight-ntwrk/credential-compact@0.2.0`: its Jubjub subgroup check
passes `(r + 1) / 8 as Field` to `ecMul`.

Root cause: the typechecker only accepts such a literal written as `N as
Field`, and it lowers that to a bare `(quote N)` with no `safe-cast`
(`analysis-passes.ss`, the `cast` Field special case). A call argument
gets its expected type only from that wrapper, so the literal reached
the emitter's `quote` clause with no type.

### Fix

In `compiler/rust-passes-emit.ss`, the integer branch of the `quote`
clause now renders the literal as `field-literal-rust`
(`Fr::from_le_bytes(...)`) when no expected type is bound and the
literal is above `(max-unsigned)`. The existing expected-type branches
are unchanged and still take precedence.

**Threshold is `max-unsigned`, not `u128::MAX` as #90 proposed.** Above
`max-unsigned` the literal can only be a `Field`, because the
typechecker admits it only through `N as Field`, so the fallback can't
give it the wrong type. A literal in `(u128::MAX, max-unsigned]` is a
valid `Uint`. Such literals already reach call arguments wrapped in a
`safe-cast`, so they keep their typed rendering. Rendering them as `Fr`
would hide the backend's missing wide-`Uint` support.

Rendering every argument at the callee's declared parameter type is the
general fix for this class of bug; that is Part 2 below. This fallback
stays as a backstop.

### Tests

- `examples/literal_coercion_fixture.compact` gets 8 new pure circuits
that use the Jubjub constant. They cover a native (`ecMul`) argument, a
pure-circuit argument, a `const`, a return value, a Field operand, an
equality operand, the 2^248 boundary, and
`ecMul(ecMul(ecMulGenerator(1), c), 8)`. The existing "huge" literals
are 2^200, below `max-unsigned`, so they never reached this code path.
- The regenerated `lib.rs` diff only adds code: +88 lines, no bare
integers above `u128::MAX`. Regenerating the pre-change fixture with the
new compiler gives byte-identical output.
- The TS reference capture was re-run and is unchanged, so it is not in
the diff.
- New test `field_only_literals_materialise_without_an_expected_type`:
- computes `(r + 1) / 8` with integer arithmetic and checks the
little-endian bytes from every position;
  - checks the 2^248 boundary bytes;
  - checks that the subgroup check returns `ecMulGenerator(1)`.

Local runs (at the time of the #90 commits):
- `./compiler/go` ✅
- `cargo fmt --check` ✅
- `cargo clippy -D warnings` ✅
- `cargo test -p midnight-compact-runtime -p tests-e2e-rust` ✅ (57
suites, incl. `codegen_regression`, `ts_rust_target_parity`,
`rejection_corpus`)

Note: the machine has no rustup, so these ran with nixpkgs `cargo` 1.95
/ `rustfmt` 1.9.0 on top of `nix develop`. That rustfmt reproduces the
committed fixtures byte-for-byte. The `compiler-backed` CI job is the
authoritative check.

### Downstream check

I compiled `midnight-vc-passport@develop` (`cb916ad`)
`packages/midnight-vc-passport/src/digital-passport-credential.compact`,
with `@midnight-ntwrk/credential-compact@0.2.0` staged the way its
`stage-core-compact.mjs` does it, using the fixed `compactc --target
rust --skip-zk`.
- `compactc` exits 0. The subgroup constant is emitted as
`Fr::from_le_bytes(...)`.
- `cargo build` of the generated crate against this repo's `runtime-rs`
succeeds.

This PR also carries the OpenSpec proposal for both changes and the
`.agents/skills` move.

589c92ef961ce89ac730140e81b76d4c08222a70.message:
## What this pins

#98 added a scan refusing any `/* TODO` marker that reaches the
generated crate. It ignores markers inside Rust **string literals** —
and I asserted that without testing it. A false positive there rejects
contracts that are perfectly fine.

The route turns out to be ordinary Compact. An `assert` message is user
text that survives into the crate verbatim:

```compact
assert(n.read() == 1, "/* TODO not a marker");
```

lands at line 108 of the emitted Rust, inside a string. **Verified: exit
0, crate emitted.** Someone writing `assert(x, "/* TODO fix this")`
would have hit a false positive had the exclusion been wrong, and
nothing would have caught it.

## Two worthless tests, recorded so they aren't repeated

I got this wrong twice before getting it right, and both failures are
instructive:

| Attempt | Why it proved nothing |
|---|---|
| `pad(32, "/* TODO ...")` | `pad` compiles its string to **bytes**. The
marker never reaches the output, so the test passes without exercising
the exclusion at all |
| `assert` with `>` | refused by `circuit-body-emission` before the
guard runs — failed for an unrelated reason |

A test that passes for the wrong reason is worse than no test, because
it reports coverage that does not exist. The first one in particular
looked like a clean pass.

## Why the other five kinds have no probe

Documented in the file, so the gaps read as decisions rather than
oversights.

**`unknown-type`, `type-variant`, `enum-ref-unresolved` are defensive.**
Each guards an IR state a well-typed program should not reach — a value
with no type, a Type variant the pass does not know, an enum-ref whose
discriminant is absent from its own enum's variant list. I could not
construct Compact source reaching any of them, which is the point of
them existing: they catch a front-end or pass bug, not a user mistake. A
probe would have to fabricate broken IR, and would then be testing the
fabrication.

**`todo-placeholder` and `sentinel-splice` are backstops** over the
finished output, for the site nobody remembered. By construction no
contract triggers them while every renderer behaves. They were verified
in #98 by injecting a marker into the prelude — a compiler-source edit,
not a contract — which belongs in a commit's evidence rather than in
this table. Their false-positive side *is* reachable, and that is what
this PR pins.

## Evidence

| | |
|---|---|
| exclusion holds | `exit=0`, `lib.rs` emitted, marker present at line
108 inside a string literal |
| marker genuinely reaches output | `grep -n TODO` on the emitted crate
confirms it, so the test is not vacuous |

Stacks on #98 (merged). Base `codegen-rust` @ `5a55db50`.

5a55db50438739afb45467fe69d04bb86e04a74b.message:
## The defects

Five sites emitted `/* TODO ... */` into the generated crate.

| Position | Sites | Fails where |
|---|---|---|
| **type** (`topaque`, `tunknown`, catch-all) | 3 | `cargo build` —
late, but loud |
| **value** (`enum-ref`) | 2 | **nowhere** |

`/* TODO M3-J2: unresolved enum-ref */ 0u8` is the dangerous one. The
crate compiles, runs, and uses discriminant zero — a constructor
comparing against the wrong variant takes the wrong branch, and nothing
ever complains.

Each site now raises `rust-feature-error`, reporting at the Compact
source with a kind: `opaque-type`, `unknown-type`, `type-variant`,
`enum-ref-unresolved`.

## The part worth reviewing: why the existing guard missed them

`flush-rust-output!` has scanned the finished `lib.rs` since task 4.1,
and the architecture was right — buffer, scan, refuse, and let the
target-port handler delete the still-empty file. I initially assumed the
systemic fix was to *port* this from the vehicle. It was already here.

**`rust-false-sentinel-index` hunts a spliced Scheme `#f`, and to avoid
false positives it skips anything inside a comment. A TODO marker *is* a
comment.** The scanner enters `/*`, skips to `*/`, resumes on `0u8` — a
legitimate token — and has nothing to object to.

So the backstop was not missing. It was watching the wrong door, and the
door it watched was the one nothing came through: there is no live
`#f`-splice defect on this line, while the marker family shipped twice.

A guard defined by *how a value fails* only catches failures shaped like
the one that motivated it. What the two modes share is the
**consequence**, so `rust-todo-marker-index` is defined by that instead:
nothing that says "I could not do this" may reach the file. Markers
inside string literals are ignored, so a contract legitimately
containing that text does not trip it.

This is what makes "we got them all" a property the build checks rather
than a claim in a commit message.

## `type-fingerprint` moves in the same change

It has to. A fingerprint is a structural **key**, not emitted Rust, so
it must stay total over every Type node. Delegating to `type-rust` was
harmless only while unlowerable types produced a placeholder; once they
refuse, computing a key for `export {Maybe}` dies on its type variable
`T`. Splitting the two would leave the branch broken in between.

## Evidence

All re-run on this branch.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| **Parity** | **34 of 34** fixtures regenerate byte-identically · 0
differing · 0 failures |
| **Rejection fires** | `Opaque<"NotAThing">` probe → `exit=255`, no
`lib.rs`, `probe.compact line 2 char 22: ... (opaque-type)` |
| **No false positive** | an ordinary contract still compiles and emits
|
| **Backstop fires** | `/* TODO */` injected into the prelude so it
reaches output → `exit=255`, no `lib.rs`, `(todo-placeholder)` |

On that last one: **my first attempt to prove it was inconclusive and I
am reporting it as such.** I restored the old placeholder at the opaque
site expecting the backstop to catch it; instead
`ledger-read-decoder-missing` caught it first, so the marker never
reached the scan and the new guard was never exercised. The prelude
injection is the version that actually tests the thing.

## Test coverage

`rejection_corpus.rs` gains an `opaque-type` probe. The harness already
asserts the three properties that matter — non-zero exit, no emitted
`lib.rs`, and a greppable kind in the diagnostic — so this is an entry,
not a new harness.

## Supersedes

#96 (type position) and #97 (value position) carried these halves
separately, before I understood that the guard already existed and why
it was blind. Close both in favour of this.

# Overview

Merges `digital-passport-support` into `codegen-rust`. The branch
fast-forwards
cleanly (16 commits, no divergence), so this is a straight integration
of the
digital-passport dogfooding work plus the Rust codegen fixes it
uncovered.

## What's in it

**Compiler / Rust codegen** (`compiler/rust-passes*.ss`)
- Type-directed expression coercion (#79) — operands are coerced to
their
  expected type at the point of use, replacing the previous ad-hoc width
  handling.
- Conditional expressions emitted in all positions (#80) — ternary/`if`
results
  now lower correctly as sub-expressions, not just statements.
- Rejection corpus and byte-parity behaviour tightened alongside.

**Compiler-backed CI enforcement** (`#77`)
- New `compiler-backed` lane in `rust-runtime-test.yml` that has both a
built
  `compactc` and a Rust toolchain, running `cargo test -p tests-e2e-rust
--locked` with **no `--skip` flags**. Previously the byte-parity test
and the
`rust_backend_*` rejection corpus were excluded by name and never
enforced
  remotely.
- New `every_fixture_crate_is_a_dev_dependency` invariant test so a
fixture row
  can't silently be invisible to the harness.

**Digital-passport dogfooding** (`#78`, `#81`)
- Vendored the digital-passport contract as a codegen oracle, with
provenance
  recorded in `PROVENANCE.md`.
- `digital-passport-credential` fixture registered and gated, plus a
`docs/adr/0003-bounded-dogfood-enclave.md` describing the scope
boundary.

**Fixtures / tests**
- New fixtures: `literal-coercion-fixture`,
`mixed-width-operand-fixture`,
`ternary-cond-fixture`, `digital-passport-credential`, each with
TS-state
  capture scripts and Rust integration tests.
- `ts-rust-target-parity` coverage extended.

**OpenSpec planning workflow**
- Added the OpenSpec change workflow (skills, `openspec/config.yaml`,
specs) and
archived the five changes applied on this branch:
`compiler-backed-ci-gate`,
  `vendor-digital-passport-harness`, `fix-ternary-expression-codegen`,
`add-digital-passport-dogfood-fixture`,
`type-directed-expression-coercion`.

## Notes for the reviewer

- The bulk of the diff (`lib.rs` oracles, captured TS state) is
generated
  fixture data — the reviewable surface is `compiler/rust-passes*.ss`,
  `rust-runtime-test.yml`, and `tests-e2e-rust/tests/*.rs`.
- `codegen-rust` is an ancestor of this branch, so merging will be a
  fast-forward.

- [x] Useful pull request description

- [x] Key commits have useful messages
- [ ] All check jobs of the CI have succeeded
- [x] Self-reviewed the diff

62c81be8e267e3290cc2f79ece26d183ad2be45b.message:
tiny.in_state(s: STATE) emitted body `decode_u8(_av)? == s`, mixing u8
(LHS, ledger decoder) and STATE (RHS, tenum-typed formal). The Rust
compiler rejects it with E0308 — the operands have different types.
Bug-9's closure made `in_state` visible, surfacing the long-latent
mismatch.

The fix decodes tenum-typed ledger reads as the typed enum rather than
as the raw u8 discriminant. Going through
`decode_via_field_repr::<EnumName>` (the user enum already derives
FromFieldRepr via H4 in rust-passes-decls.ss) keeps both sides of the
`==` in the same Rust type. The walker's existing tenum-name-of-type
check on the `==` IR drives the RHS enum-ref to render as
`EnumName::variant`, so the comparison now reads
`decode_via_field_repr::<STATE>(_av)? == s`.

This is Option A from the analysis — preferred over Option B (var-ref
`as u8` cast) and Option C (refining Bug-8's special case) because it
eliminates the integer-coercion regression rather than patching around
it. tenum-typed reads no longer trigger Bug-8's integer short-circuit;
Boolean and Uint ledger reads still flow through decode_bool /
decode_uN and keep Bug-8 in force.

Three places change:

1. rust-passes-emit.ss decoder-for-type's tenum arm now emits
   `decode_via_field_repr::<EnumName>` instead of `decode_u8`. Both the
   Ledger struct accessor (`pub fn state(&self) -> Result<STATE, _>`)
   and emit-ledger-read-expr (inline gather block in expression
   position) flow through this helper, so the change is uniform.

2. rust-passes-walker.ss is-ledger-read-expr? now exempts ledger reads
   whose result type is a tenum (via the new helper
   adt-op-tenum-result?). Bug-8's short-circuit was designed for u8
   decoders; with the typed decoder in place, tenum reads must
   participate in typed-enum rendering on the opposite operand.

3. rust-passes-walker.ss inline-circuit-call now renders each formal's
   actual under current-enum-ref-typed? when the formal's declared type
   is a tenum. tiny's `assert(in_state(STATE.unset), ...)` inlines into
   `state == STATE.unset`; without this, the eager actual-rendering at
   formal-bind time would resolve `STATE.unset` to `0u8` before the
   body's `==` walker sees it, leaving the LHS-typed/RHS-u8 mismatch
   in place. Threading the typed flag through the actual-rendering
   keeps the formal substitution honest.

Cross-references:
- Bug-4 (2026-06-24): added the tenum-name-of-type heuristic on the
  `==` IR's type field; necessary for did.compact's
  `disclosed_mutation == MapMutation.Insert`.
- Bug-8 (2026-06-26): added is-ledger-read-expr? short-circuit to
  preserve integer-typed comparisons for non-tenum ledger reads.
  Bug-10's helper extends that short-circuit so it only fires for
  integer-typed reads, leaving tenum reads to the new typed decoder.

67f7cbc8b2ea3164d9fb225c7f9fd67a9aa3d552.description: Retained eight-file Ltypescript text-emission suite; compiler/rust-passes.ss, compiler/rust-passes-walker.ss, compiler/README-rust-passes.md.
67f7cbc8b2ea3164d9fb225c7f9fd67a9aa3d552.message:
The print-rust pass that walks the Ltypescript IR and emits a Rust
crate consuming `compact-runtime`. Split across 7 includes loaded by
rust-passes.ss for readability — see compiler/README-rust-passes.md
for the module map.

Module breakdown:

- rust-passes.ss (~100 LOC) — entry point. Defines the print-rust
  pass + the Program clause that drives top-level emission ordering
  (typedefs → witnesses → contract struct → initial-state → impure
  circuits → ledger view → Cargo.toml).
- rust-passes-helpers.ss (~250 LOC) — identifier helpers (casing,
  sym ⇄ rust id), fluid parameters (current-formal-arg-types,
  current-ledger-field-types, current-loop-var-substitutions,
  current-arith-suffix), stdlib lookup tables, uniquify-rust-name
  for tmp gensym, rust-feature-error for compile-time hard-fail
  on unsupported Compact constructs.
- rust-passes-types.ss (~210 LOC) — `type-rust` (Ltypescript Type →
  Rust type string) + per-field Aligned / FieldRepr / FromFieldRepr
  emission helpers. Handles primitives (Field, Boolean, Bytes<N>,
  Vector<N,T>, Uint<8..128>, Uint<L..U>), tuples, transparent +
  nominal aliases, user struct/enum references, Maybe<T>.
- rust-passes-prelude.ss (~250 LOC) — file header (full Apache-2.0
  + Midnight Foundation copyright matching add_headers.py), the
  `#![allow(...)]` blanket for codegen-emitted code, witness trait
  emission, contract-struct shell, program-* IR collectors.
- rust-passes-decls.ss (~340 LOC) — collect-pure-circuit-tdefns +
  emit-type-decls (user enums and structs with their Aligned /
  FieldRepr / FromFieldRepr impls, including BinaryHashRepr for hash
  argument shaping).
- rust-passes-walker.ss (~2400 LOC) — body walker. body-walkable?
  predicates + emit-body-or-fallback central dispatch — translates
  Compact statements to Rust expressions on the OpProgramVerify /
  OpProgramGather builder chain. Carries constructor body emission,
  for-range / for-iter / fold compile-time unrolling with loop-var
  substitution, witness threading, defensive .clone() for var-ref
  args at call sites, enum-aware ==, struct-literal lowering,
  cross-circuit calls, ADT method emission (.insert / .lookup /
  .member / .checkRoot / etc.). The main hub — most circuit-body
  features land here.
- rust-passes-streaming.ss (~520 LOC) — multi-stage body walker for
  bodies that interleave gather (read) and verify (write) ops, plus
  mid-body if-statements that mix the two.
- rust-passes-emit.ss (~1850 LOC) — emit-initial-state with
  ADT-aware seeding (new_cell / new_map / new_list / new_merkle_tree
  / new_historic_merkle_tree / new_cell_bounded_uint for non-power-
  of-2 byte widths) + circuit body assembly + ledger-view emission.
  Renders the actual Rust text — VM-instruction → builder-method
  translations live here. Carries literal-RHS coercion that produces
  `Fr::from(N)` for Field-typed integer literals and `Nu8/u16/u32/
  u64/u128` for unsigned-integer-typed literals.

README-rust-passes.md — module map + "how a new feature lands" recipe
+ "when something breaks" failure-mode table. Reading order for new
contributors: this README → rust-passes-types.ss → the walker's
body-walkable? + emit-body-or-fallback → one specific fixture's
lib.rs to see actual output.

Coverage at this layer: scalars + ADTs (Counter / Cell / Map / Set /
MerkleTree / HistoricMerkleTree / List), user structs + enums,
transparent + nominal aliases, witnesses, native hashes, if-statement
bodies, ADT method calls, cross-circuit calls, for-range / for-
iterable / fold with compile-time unrolling, basic map() with non-
identity lambdas (wrapping_* arithmetic + downcast_unsigned), bounded
Uint<L..U>, sealed ledger fields. Frontend desugaring covers modules
+ generics — no codegen work needed for either (verified via
fixtures).

Unsupported Compact constructs produce `compactc --rust: unsupported
Compact construct (FEATURE_TAG): ...` at compactc time rather than
emitting `unimplemented!()` Rust that panics at runtime. Feature tags
cover the known gaps.

6aa3cdcd09fc8ab27836dbf26cce02de98dd5be6.message:
Closes the Walker A21 gap so `compactc --rust` accepts a circuit body
that calls `t.insertIndexDefault(idx)` on a `HistoricMerkleTree<H, T>`.
Before this commit, the walker rejected the body with
`circuit-body-emission: no walker shape matched` because the vm-code
for `insertIndexDefault` contains the bounded-index branch sequence
(`lt`, `branch`, `jmp`, `swap`, `pop`) and a `(rt-null value_type)`
default that `vm-cell-elem->rust` couldn't render.

The existing `emit-non-write-public-ledger-terminal` already routes
ADT update ops through `expand-vm-code` + `vminstr->builder-call`
(the I3a path used by `HMT.insert`); A21 simply broadens that
machinery to cover the richer vm-code shape `insertIndexDefault`
emits — no new walker shape was required.

Changes
-------

runtime-rs/src/op_builder.rs
  - OpProgramVerify gains five new builder methods: `lt`, `branch`,
    `jmp`, `swap`, `pop`. Each is a thin wrapper around the matching
    `Op<ResultModeVerify, D>` variant — the underlying VM ops already
    exist in midnight-onchain-vm 3.1.0; the codegen just needed the
    Rust-side builder surface to call them.

compiler/rust-passes-emit.ss
  - `vm-cell-elem->rust` learns `VMnull T` → `default-value-rust(T)`,
    matching the TS reference's `default(value_type)` rendering. This
    is what `(rt-leaf-hash (rt-null value_type))` reduces to after
    `expand-vm-code` substitutes the HMT element type, so the push
    becomes
    `new_cell(leaf_hash(&ValueReprAlignedValue(AlignedValue::from(0u8))))`
    for `HistoricMerkleTree<H, Uint<8>>`.

  - `vminstr->builder-call` learns the five branching / stack-
    shuffling ops the bounded-index `insert*Index*` vm-code emits.
    Each renders 1:1 onto the new OpProgramVerify builder methods —
    `query_for_verify` walks the resulting program with the same VM
    semantics as the TS reference, preserving byte-parity without
    recovering structured control flow at the Rust source level.

Scope
-----

This is a vm-code-level closure — the shape is generic enough to also
unlock `HMT.insertIndex`, `HMT.insertHash`, `HMT.insertHashIndex` and
the matching `MerkleTree.insert*Index*` ops (all share the same
`(dup 1)(dup 1)(lt)(branch …)(pop)(jmp …)(swap 0)(pop)` cleanup).
A20's byte-parity guard for those families will need to be added in
a follow-up fixture (this commit's companion adds the HMT default
one); the regression net widens automatically as soon as a contract
exercises them.

7072f3c8a7936d3871a01392d72efa6305142028.message:
## Problem

`compact_runtime::std_lib::decode_via_field_repr<T>`
(runtime-rs/src/std_lib/adts.rs) converted `AlignedValue` atoms to `Fr`s
**1:1** — one `Fr::try_from(atom)` per atom — and fed the result to
`T::from_field_repr`. But cells are **alignment-encoded**: one atom per
leaf value, and a single leaf may span multiple field-repr `Fr`s.

Verified empirically in MediaNoxLabs/midnight-identity (the **"second
decode-path finding"** in the MediaNoxLabs/compact#3 comment thread):

- **`ContractAddress { bytes: Bytes<32> }`**: the cell is ONE 32-byte
atom, but `[u8; 32]::FIELD_SIZE == 2` `Fr`s (repr[0] = the 1-byte stray
tail chunk, repr[1] = the leading 31-byte chunk — upstream `impl
FieldRepr for [u8]` packs from the end with `FR_BYTES_STORED = 31`). 1
Fr != 2 -> `from_field_repr` returns `None` -> `ledger().id()` and the
did-05 constructor's `id = kernel.self()` readback could **never**
succeed. MediaNoxLabs/compact#4 landed the did-05 readback gate
`#[ignore]`d on exactly this bug.
- **Struct map values**: a `VerificationMethod` cell is 6 atoms
(id-utf8, typ, kty, crv, x-utf8, y-utf8) but its `FIELD_SIZE` is 3 — the
same arity mismatch for in-circuit map lookups.

## Fix (runtime-rs only — zero codegen changes)

`decode_via_field_repr` now walks `av.alignment` in lockstep with the
value's atoms and expands each leaf into exactly the `Fr` chunks its
field-repr occupies:

| Alignment atom | Expansion |
|---|---|
| `Field` | one `Fr` via `Fr::try_from` (unchanged) |
| `Bytes { length }` | `ceil(length/31)` 31-byte LE chunks in reverse
chunk order; leading zero-`Fr`s re-pad the trailing zero bytes stripped
by `ValueAtom::normalize` (same rule as upstream
`ValueAtom::field_repr_unchecked`) |
| `Compress` (opaque string / `Vec<u8>`) | raw-byte chunks of the actual
atom: `ceil(n/31)` `Fr`s, **zero** `Fr`s for the empty value — matching
this runtime's `OpaqueString`/`Vec<u8>` `FieldRepr` convention (raw
bytes, not upstream's non-invertible transient-commit hash) |
| `Option` segments | mirror upstream `Value::repr_traverse` (2-byte
discriminant, chosen variant, zero-`Fr` padding to the widest variant) |

**Empty-atom decision**: an empty `Compress` atom (e.g. JWK `y=""`)
expands to **zero** `Fr`s — `[u8]::field_repr` of `[]` emits nothing,
and `OpaqueString::FIELD_SIZE == 0` + `vec_u8_from_field_repr(&[]) ==
Some(vec![])` rely on exactly this, so no minimum-1-Fr behavior is
needed (verified by round-trip tests, incl. the did-05 `y=""` shape).
Empty `Bytes{N}` atoms (all-zero integers/addresses) re-pad to
`ceil(N/31)` zero `Fr`s from the *declared* alignment width.

`OpaqueString::from_field_repr` additionally strips the 31-byte-chunk
zero padding: on-chain `Compress` atoms must be normal-form, so trailing
NULs are unrepresentable in the cell encoding and stripping is the
faithful inverse.

`decode_jubjub_point` is untouched — point cells are 2 `Field` atoms ->
2 `Fr`s, already correct (now also covered by a round-trip test).

### Known limitation (reported, not silently special-cased)

A **non-empty** variable-length leaf inside a fixed-slicing struct
cannot round-trip through `from_field_repr`: generated code slices
string fields at `OpaqueString::FIELD_SIZE == 0`, so there is no slot to
carry the bytes. The decoder therefore enforces `expanded len ==
T::FIELD_SIZE` for fixed-size targets and **fails loudly** instead of
silently mis-slicing every following field. Struct string leaves
round-trip exactly while empty; non-empty ones (e.g. a
`VerificationMethod` with a real `id`) need a codegen follow-up
(variable-size-aware `from_field_repr` slicing). The did-05 circuits'
own map-lookup consumers only read the non-string fields
(`publicKeyJwk.crv`, `publicKey`), so this surfaces as a clean error
rather than wrong data.

## Tests

- **Round-trip unit tests** (`runtime-rs/src/std_lib/adts.rs`),
invariant `decode_via_field_repr::<T>(new_cell(T).cell_av()) == T`:
u8/u32/u64/bool/`Fr`, tuple, `ContractAddress` (incl. all-zero ->
normalised-empty-atom edge and trailing-zero tails), `[u8; 32]`, a `[u8;
32]`-bearing struct, a JWK-shaped multi-leaf struct with empty string
leaves, plain enums (variant 0 = empty atom), opaque strings (empty /
1-byte / <31 / exactly-31 / multi-chunk >31), the loud
non-empty-string-leaf rejection, and `decode_jubjub_point`.
- **did-05 readback gate flipped**
(`tests-e2e-rust/tests/did05_constructor_scaffold.rs`): the full
executing `initial_state` -> `ledger()` accessor readback from
MediaNoxLabs/compact#4 is un-ignored and **passes**, now including `id`
read back via `ledger().id()` (the constructor writes `kernel.self()`);
the pre-A30 failure-mode pin test is removed.
- **Full e2e suite green** including `codegen_regression` byte-parity
against the rebuilt `nix build .#compactc` (0.31.110): **zero fixture
drift** — the fix changes no generated code.

## Versioning

Toolchain 0.31.109 -> **0.31.110** (`compiler/compiler-version.ss`,
`flake.nix`, `doc/ledger-adt.mdx`, `CHANGELOG.md`). The runtime crate
stays **0.16.100**: generated contracts pin it via
`check_runtime_version!` with exact string equality, so a runtime crate
bump would either break every existing generated contract or force a
regeneration (fixture drift) — the version guards do not distinguish
runtime-only behavior changes, hence only the toolchain version advances
and the CHANGELOG entry records the runtime-side fix.

## Gates

- `nix build .#compactc` OK (reports 0.31.110)
- `cargo fmt --all --check` OK; `cargo clippy -p
{compact-runtime,compact-runtime-macros,tests-e2e-rust} --all-targets
--all-features -- -D warnings` OK
- `cargo test -p compact-runtime --locked` OK (24 adts tests, 13 new)
- `cargo test -p tests-e2e-rust --locked` OK (incl. byte-parity, 0
ignored)

## Branch and ledger policy

**This branch stays on ledger 9.** It is the forward track and matches
upstream `main`'s own flake pin — upstream pins
`github:midnightntwrk/midnight-ledger/ledger-9.1.0.0-rc.3` on `zkir`,
`onchain-runtime-v4` and `zkir-wasm`, and our `flake.lock` resolves all
three to the same rev `4823b5351b17cc49e30f19760dbd30a73cf95e22` as
`Cargo.lock`'s git dependency. Ledger 9 is expected to release within a
couple of months.

**`codegen-rust` is untouched and stays on the released ledger-8 line.**
It is what the downstream consumer (`MediaNoxLabs/midnight-identity`)
pins, and it resolves real chain state against live networks — where
`ContractState` is still tagged `[v6]`.

A consequence worth stating plainly: **the two branches can never share
`ContractState`-level fixtures.** Ledger-8 networks emit
`midnight:contract-state[v6]:`; this branch emits and expects `[v8]`. A
crossed fixture fails loudly (`InvalidData: expected header tag …`),
never mis-decodes, so this is a maintenance cost rather than a
correctness risk. See "Follow-ups" for the way out.
