## Conflict resolutions

Verified against `git diff 56c3b77 e9d8b1a` (upstream merge-base vs. the
merge commit).

**`analysis-passes/expand-modules-and-types.ss`** — the fork's M3.5-E2
block (auto-promotes user struct/enum types reachable from public
surfaces into synthetic `export-typedef`s so the Rust struct emitter can
see them) survived the file split intact. It is the first form inside
the `(let ([reachable* (process-frob-worklist …)])`, so `reachable*` is
populated and `exported-type*` is still mutable, and it stays wrapped in
`(when (emit-rust) …)`. Body is textually identical to the pre-merge
copy modulo indentation.

**`compiler/passes.ss`** — the fork's `prepare-for-typescript-passes` /
`print-typescript-passes` split (which shares one `Ltypescript` IR
between the TS and Rust emitters) was rebuilt on top of upstream's tail.
Checked that `--final-pass` still escapes correctly (the `quit`
continuation is captured once in `generate-everything`, outside both
pass lists) and that `print-typescript`'s nine mutation sites are all
pass-local, so `--rust` and `--rust --skip-ts` produce identical Rust.

**`natives.ss` / `midnight-natives.ss`** — the fork's `(rust "...")`
annotation form and the extra `native-entry` field survived upstream's
`np`→`pt` metavariable rename cleanly. Sorted `(rust "…"` sets pre-merge
vs. merged differ by exactly `+ (rust "compact_runtime::ec_neg")`;
nothing was dropped.

**One resolution was wrong and is fixed here** — see the first bullet
under Fixed defects.

## IR port table

Upstream reshaped several `Ltypescript` productions the `--rust` backend
pattern-matches on, which is what broke `nix build .#compactc`.

| Production | Before | After | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `+` `-` `*` | `(… src mbits e1 e2)` | `(… src type e1 e2)` | Retired
`mbits->rust-width` for `arith-result-rust-width`, which reuses the
existing `uint-rust-width` ladder instead of adding a second one |
| `downcast-unsigned` | `(… src (maybe nat?) nat e)` | `(… src nat2 nat1
e)` | Slot rename; target bound is still the second slot. Zero behaviour
change |
| `cast-from-field` | *(was `downcast-unsigned` with `nat? = #f`)* | `(…
src nat ftype e)` | Now **rejected** with a diagnostic — see Fixed
defects |
| `cast-to-field` | *(new)* | `(… src ftype type e)` |
`Field`/`Uint<N≤64> as JubjubScalar` →
`compact_runtime::jubjub_scalar_from_field`; reverse direction rejected
|
| `tfield` | `(tfield src)` | `(tfield src ftype)` | `field-type-rust`
maps `field-native`→`Fr`, `field-scalar (curve-jubjub)`→`JubjubScalar` |
| `tpoint` | `(topaque src "JubjubPoint")` | `(tpoint src ctype)` | Same
decoder + default-seeding routing as the old spelling |
| program node | `(program src ((ex n)…) tdescs …)` | `+ (contract-type*
…)` | Matched and ignored (no cross-contract-call support) |
| `ecMul`/`ecMulGenerator`/`ecNeg` | `Field` scalar | `JubjubScalar`;
`ecNeg` added | Runtime + natives bindings |

Confirmed **not** on our path, so no work: `native-type`/`ntdecl` and
`serialize`/`deserialize` are both removed before `Ltypescript`;
`contract-implements`/`cidecl` never reaches the program node we match;
`tcontract` becoming a `Contract-Type` nonterminal alternative still
matches our existing `nanopass-case` clauses (upstream's own post-change
code does the same).

### The `(not mbits)` guards — deliberately translated literally

Six walker guards read `(and (not mbits) …)`. Checking the pre-0.33
typer (`origin/develop:compiler/analysis-passes.ss:2126` and `:2155`),
`mbits` was `(max 1 (integer-length result-nat))` for **Uint** results
and `#f` for **Field** results — so the literal translation is
`(type-is-tfield? type)`, and that is what ships.

It is also, on inspection, **inverted relative to its own intent**:
`arith-binop-rust` emits `.wrapping_*`, which `Fr` does not implement,
so these guards should admit `tunsigned` and reject `tfield`. Every
fixture that emits `wrapping_*` today has a Uint result type and reaches
the emitter through the constructor / `seq-stmt` / `cond-rust` routes
rather than through these predicates — i.e. the guards are effectively
dead. Flipping them is expected to *move* fixture bytes, so it is left
as an isolated follow-up rather than smuggled into an integration
commit. The zero-drift regen below is the evidence that the literal
translation is byte-parity-neutral.

## Fixed defects

**Cross-contract calls did not compile at all.** Upstream's new
`circuit-passes/desugar-contract-calls.ss` synthesises a
`transientCommit` native by calling `make-native-entry` with 4
arguments, but the fork's record has five fields (it carries
`rust-function`). Every cross-contract-call test died with `incorrect
number of arguments 4 to #<procedure make-native-entry>` — **47
failures** across `save-contract-info` (77/110), `print-zkir` (174/175),
`print-zkir-v3` (183/184) and `save-manifest` (682/695). Filled the slot
with `compact_runtime::transient_commit`, the binding `transientCommit`
already declares. This was a genuine merge-resolution miss, found only
by running `./compiler/go`.

**`Field as Uint<N>` emitted Rust that cannot compile.** The shared
`downcast-unsigned` clause rendered `(<expr>) as uN` regardless of
source type, so a Field source produced `(f) as u64` with `f: Fr`. `Fr`
is a struct, and Rust's `as` only casts between primitives, so that is
E0605 "non-primitive cast" — compactc exited 0 and the breakage surfaced
only at `cargo build`. It is now rejected with a diagnostic. Lowering it
properly needs a range-checking `compact_runtime` helper.

**`--rust` + `--feature-zkir-v3` produced broken output.** The v3
natives carry no `(rust …)` bindings and the v3-only type surface has no
lowering, so `compiler/rust-passes-types.ss` mapped `curve-secp256k1` to
literal Rust *comment strings* (`"/* TODO zkir-v3: Secp256k1Point */"`)
emitted where a type must go. A contract using a v3 *type* without
calling a v3 *native* therefore compiled to a `lib.rs` that does not
parse. Now rejected up front in **both** `compactc.ss` (friendly CLI
message) and `generate-everything` in `passes.ss` — the latter matters
because `compiler/test.ss` parameterizes `emit-rust` directly and never
goes through the CLI. Note the merge commit had already shipped a
comment in `zkir-v3-natives.ss` asserting this guard existed; it did not
until now.

**TypeScript-path divergence closed.** The fork's F8 patch passed an
alias's `nominal?` flag through `apply-type-alias` unconditionally,
where upstream passes `#f`. It is now gated on `(emit-rust)` per ADR
0002, so the TS pipeline sees exactly upstream's IR. Rust output is
unchanged.

Also corrected three stale comments that documented behaviour the code
does not have: `natives.ss` and `rust-passes-prelude.ss` both claimed
unmapped natives "fall back to a TODO comment" (they hard-error via
`rust-feature-error`), and `rust-passes-helpers.ss` claimed stdlib
circuits are excluded from `program-circuits` (the filter only excludes
*non-exported* ones — what actually keeps `jubjubSchnorrVerify`'s body
away from the walker is that it is generic and rewritten at the call
site).

```
  32 +compact_runtime::check_runtime_version!("0.18.107");

```

Every fixture changed by exactly one line: the runtime-version pin.
**This is the load-bearing evidence for the whole IR port** — the
`mbits`→`type` migration, the literal `(not mbits)` translation, the
`tfield`+ftype / `tpoint` / program-node changes and the
`downcast-unsigned` slot rename are all provably byte-parity-neutral.
The two `print-rust` snapshots
(`compiler/snapshots/{tiny,counter}-rust-expected.rs.txt`) change the
same single line.

`digital-passport` has no in-tree `.compact` source and is not
regenerable; it keeps its hand-applied `jubjub_scalar_from_field(…)`
wrappers around `ec_mul`/`ec_mul_generator`, which I checked match what
the new `cast-to-field` clause emits.

### Two `.compact` sources needed an edit

Upstream 0.33 no longer implicitly widens an integer literal to `Field`
in ledger-assignment position:

```
Exception: sealed_ledger_fixture.compact line 75 char 9:
  expected right-hand side of = to have type Field but received Uint<0..43>
```

Reproduced without `--rust`, so it is a language change, not a backend
one. `sealed_ledger_fixture.compact` and
`struct_collision_fixture.compact` gained explicit `as Field` casts — a
`safe-cast` that lowers to the same `Fr::from(<n>u64)`, which is why
both fixtures still show only the version-line diff.

### TS references — 27/27 re-captured, per-fixture justification

All were stale: ledger 9 moved the envelope tag from
`contract-state[v6]` to `[v8]`, and the tag is a literal ASCII prefix in
the bytes, so every `*_init_byte_parity` test failed before reaching the
payload.

**Nothing was hand-edited.** Each JSON was regenerated by re-running its
capture script against the ledger-9 TS runtime. Classifying every
`stateHex` blob old-vs-new:

- **aliases, if-stmt, vector** — payload **byte-identical**, tag only.
Direct confirmation that `charged-state[v1]` and
`impact-state-value[v2]` did not move between ledger 8 and 9.
- **all others** — tag plus the operations map. `ContractOperation` went
from one field to three (`v2`/`v3` verifier keys plus `ir`) and
`ContractMaintenanceAuthority.committee` changed element type to the new
Schnorr-or-ECDSA `ContractMaintenanceVerifyingKey`; that is what bumped
the parent tag v6→v8. The Rust side produces the matching encoding
through `ContractOperation::new(None, None)`, which is why the tests
pass.

Capture-path repairs that made this possible:

- **`capture-election.mjs`'s `runChain` was still synchronous.** Circuit
wrappers became `async` in runtime 0.17.104, so `runner(ctx)` returned a
Promise, `out.context` was `undefined`, and the surrounding `try/catch`
recorded `{error: …}` for every chain. Made it `async`, awaited each
step and each of the 5 top-level calls.
- **The wrappers no longer set `callContext.circuitId`.** The linear
scripts already stamped it; the election chain runner did not, so every
step ran under `'constructor'`. Now stamped per step.
- **`@midnight-ntwrk/onchain-runtime-v3` no longer exists** — both
importers moved to `@midnightntwrk/onchain-runtime-v4` (no hyphen after
"midnight"). zerocash keeps the direct import rather than routing
through `cr.`, because the low-level `persistentHash(align, val)` it
needs is shadowed in the compact-runtime index by the high-level
`persistentHash(rtType, value)`.

**Added `capture-counter.mjs`.** `counter` was the one fixture in the
corpus that never had a capture script (`git log --all --diff-filter=A`
finds none), so its reference had no regeneration recipe at all and the
ledger bump would have left `tests/counter.rs` permanently stale or
ignored. It is the smallest contract in the set, so writing the script
closes a long-standing hole rather than gating a test off.

**No test is `#[ignore]`d and no gate was removed.**

## Follow-ups (none blocking)

**Prioritised.**

1. **Flip the inverted `(not mbits)` → `type-is-tfield?` guards** to
`tunsigned`-only. Expected to move fixture bytes, so it needs its own
diff and its own regen.
2. **Events / `emit` have no Rust lowering.** 0.33 added the production
ungated by any `--feature` flag; the runtime half changed too
(`ResultMode::process_log` and `GatherEvent::Log` now carry
`VersionedLogItem` with an 11-variant `LogEventType`). Our generated
code absorbs the type change silently because it only matches `Read`
with a wildcard fallback. Note `MAX_LOG_EMITTED = 1 KiB` — larger events
are silently swallowed by the VM. Needs a `compact_runtime` event-append
primitive first.
3. **Move the byte-parity envelope down to `ChargedState`.**
`charged-state[v1]` and `impact-state-value[v2]` are unchanged across
ledger 8→9, structurally as well as by tag (`StateValue` and `RcMap`
both diff clean), and this PR's aliases/if-stmt/vector captures confirm
it empirically. The envelope is already synthetic in places
(`tests/for_iter_fixture.rs:60-74` hand-builds a `ContractState` purely
to match the capture shape). Capturing one layer down would make the
whole corpus ledger-version-agnostic and shareable with `codegen-rust`,
converting a permanent 27-fixture fork into a one-time re-capture.
4. **`schnorr_verify_jubjub` disagrees with the vendored circuit.**
`runtime-rs/src/std_lib/schnorr.rs` reduces the challenge `mod
r_jubjub`; `examples/did-05/jubjub-schnorr/src/schnorr.compact:50-59`
truncates to 248 bits. Since `2^248 < r_jubjub` they differ whenever
`cFull ≥ 2^248` — essentially always. No test covers it (did-05's tests
are constructor-scaffold/readback only). The Rust side already matches
the **0.33 stdlib** verifier, so the fix is a coordinated migration off
the vendored module together with `midnight-identity`, not a local
patch. The vendored module must stay for now: different challenge
derivation means existing signatures only validate under the truncation
scheme, the stdlib has no replacement for `schnorrChallengeDigest`, and
the return types differ (`[]`-asserting vs `Boolean`).
5. **`Field as Uint<N>`** needs a range-checking `compact_runtime`
helper before it can be un-rejected.
6. **ZKIR v3 Rust support** — rejected for now, deliberately out of
scope.
7. **`compact_runtime::zswap` re-exports a stubbed verifier.**
`default-features = false` drops `proof-verifying`, so `well_formed()`
is `{ Ok(()) }`. Documented loudly on the re-export in this PR; the real
fix is narrowing the re-export, which is a downstream-visible API
change.
8. **Proof-system crates resolve newer than upstream tested at this
tag** (`midnight-circuits` 6.2.1→6.3.0 / 7.2.1→7.2.4, `midnight-proofs`
0.7.2→0.7.3 / 0.8.1→0.8.2, `midnight-zk-stdlib` 1.2.1→1.3.0 /
2.3.1→2.3.5), picked up by re-resolving semver-compatible registry deps.
Impact is nil today (we build zswap without proving), but pinning to
upstream's tested set would remove a variable from future proof-path
work.
9. **`[patch.crates-io]` is load-bearing for downstream consumers.**
Building a generated contract crate *outside* this workspace fails with
`midnight_transient_crypto::proofs::VerifierKey: Serializable is not
satisfied` — the dual old/new transient-crypto (upstream's own design,
to hold a zkir-v2 and a zkir-v3 verifier key side by side) only unifies
with the patch section present. Worth documenting in the user guide once
ledger 9 ships.
10. **Gas-limit rejection semantics changed** — `gas_cost > gas_limit`
became the component-wise `!gas_cost.within_bounds(&gas_limit)`. Our
tests pass `gas_limit: None` so are blind to it; consumers that set a
limit will see different accept/reject boundaries.
11. **MerkleTree behaviour changes are untested** — out-of-bounds update
indices are now rejected instead of updating the rightmost leaf, and
indexing a collapsed tree returns `None` instead of panicking. Both are
improvements over silent corruption, but nothing in our suite pins them.

776d83e35e98417e25317bcb5d4caed74281c383.message:
Adds the byte-parity regression net for A21 — the
HistoricMerkleTree.insertIndexDefault walker closure. Before A21,
this fixture wouldn't even build (compactc rejected the circuit body
with `no walker shape matched`). After A21, the regression net
asserts each step of the post-init mutation sequence serialises to
the same `ContractState` bytes as the TS reference.

Fixture shape
-------------

  examples/hmt_default_fixture.compact
    Single contract — one HMT<3, Uint<8>> ledger field plus one
    exported circuit `add_default(idx)` that calls
    `t.insertIndexDefault(disclose(idx))`. Disclosure is required
    because `idx` flows into the path of a public-ledger write and
    Compact's witness-disclosure check kicks in unconditionally.

  tests-e2e-rust/contracts/hmt-default-fixture/
    Codegen output of `compactc --skip-zk --rust …`. Renders the
    bounded-index branch sequence verbatim — `.lt().branch(2).pop()
    .jmp(2).swap(0).pop()` — plus the default-leaf push
    (`leaf_hash(... AlignedValue::from(0u8) ...)`) that the A21
    `vm-cell-elem->rust` `VMnull` case produces for the Uint<8>
    value type.

  tests-e2e-rust/fixtures/capture-hmt-default-fixture.mjs
    Node.js driver that exercises the TS contract for three steps
    (init → add_default(0n) → add_default(2n)) and emits the
    captured ContractState hex for each. The two `add_default`
    calls both take the `lt` taken-branch arm: index + 1 (1, then
    3) is always greater than the current first_free (0, then 1).
    The fallthrough `swap/pop` arm — exercised by inserting at a
    sub-current index — would need an extra step; that's deferred
    until a future walker iteration needs it as a regression.

  tests-e2e-rust/fixtures/hmt-default-fixture-ts-state.json
    The captured bytes themselves, checked in as the contract.

  tests-e2e-rust/tests/hmt_default_fixture.rs
    Three #[test] cases — one per step — each invoking the Rust
    `Contract` and asserting `tagged_serialize` produces the same
    bytes as the TS capture. A regression on any of the new
    OpProgramVerify builder methods (`lt`/`branch`/`jmp`/`swap`/
    `pop`) or on `VMnull → default-value-rust` would surface as a
    byte mismatch at the failing step.

Wiring
------

  Cargo.toml + tests-e2e-rust/Cargo.toml
    Register the new contract crate as a workspace member and a
    test-time dev-dependency.

  tests-e2e-rust/tests/codegen_regression.rs
    Add the new fixture to `FIXTURES` so the codegen guard re-runs
    `compactc --rust` against the source and asserts the emitted
    lib.rs is byte-identical to the committed one — catching any
    future Scheme-side drift that would silently change the
    rendered op chain.

Results
-------

  cargo test -p tests-e2e-rust --tests \\
    -- --skip rust_codegen_byte_parity
    → 46 passed (was 43, A20 baseline); +3 new HMT-default cases.
  cargo clippy -p compact-runtime -p tests-e2e-rust --all-targets
    -- -D warnings → clean.
  cargo fmt --all → no diff.

The codegen_regression test is unrelated to A21 and was already
failing before this branch due to pre-existing drift on most
checked-in fixtures (`pub(crate)` visibility tweaks elsewhere in
the codegen). The new hmt-default-fixture's regen does match its
committed lib.rs byte-for-byte; that part of the codegen guard
works as designed.

792f2f206e05df35565716ea5aba87eb7696c4a0.message:
Follow-up to f3a98aa, which removed two. streaming.ss:256 had a third of
the same shape that I missed by grepping for "TODO A14" rather than for
the pattern:

  (guard (c [#t "/* TODO A24 */"]) (ctor-expr-rust …))

Same defect as the A14 pair: `[#t …]` matches every condition, so a
deliberate `rust-feature-error` was caught and replaced by a comment
emitted where an expression belongs, and a genuine emitter bug became a
comment instead of a stack trace.

That is now all three of the guards that SUBSTITUTE A STRING INTO THE
OUTPUT.

Correction to a claim in f3a98aa's message and in #33: this is not "all
catch-all guards". Grepping the pattern rather than the marker turns up
~31 more of the form

  (guard (c [#t #f]) …)

which are a different thing — they return a sentinel the caller branches
on, rather than substituting output. That is a defensible try-and-fall-back
probe idiom and those are deliberately left alone here.

They do share a root cause with the `rendered-has-todo?` string-sniffing
net, though, and it is worth stating: unsupported-ness is not represented
as a type. Because a deliberate rejection and a genuine bug raise
indistinguishable conditions, a probe has no choice but to catch
everything — so a nanopass dispatch error reads as "not supported here".
Filed separately rather than fixed, since it is a design change.

Byte-parity green and unchanged, 48 test groups, ./compiler/go exit 0 with
zero failures.

7d819588184ad3a12dfb984c7c1ffaeabf72bffe.message:
Delivers the correctness and documentation half of the audit in #33.
Closes #34, #35, #36, #37, and part 1 of #39.

Every change here is **byte-parity-neutral** — verified, not assumed.
The corpus reached none of these paths, which is also why they survived
so long.

## The correctness half

The backend's central safety property is that a construct it cannot
lower **fails the compile** rather than emitting something plausible.
Four places violated it, each producing valid, compiling, wrong Rust:

| Was | Became |
|---|---|
| constructor `assert` with a non-inlinable call → `/* TODO */ true` |
`assert!(true)` — a precondition that silently never fires |
| constructor `if`, same situation → `/* TODO */ true` | then-branch
unconditional, else-branch dead; a conditional ledger write becomes
unconditional |
| `(guard (c [#t "/* TODO A14 */"]) …)` ×2, plus a third `A24` | catches
**every** condition, so a deliberate `rust-feature-error` was replaced
by a comment emitted where an expression belongs — and genuine emitter
bugs became a comment instead of a trace |
| 4 of 17 natives carrying `(rust "… unimplemented!()")` | compiled
clean, panicked at run time |

The natives fix is structural rather than a special case: the `(rust …)`
clause is **optional** and `native-call-site-rust` *already* rejects on
a `#f` field, so dropping the clause makes absence representable as
absence and the existing rejection fires. A future unbound native cannot
emit a panic by accident — there is no string left for it to hide in.

**Verified against the built compiler:**

```
keccak256 (--feature-zkir-v3):
  unsupported Compact construct (native-binding-missing):
  no Rust binding for native function __compactRuntime.keccak256

constructor assert on a non-inlinable circuit:
  probe.compact line 11 char 10: unsupported Compact construct
  (ctor-assert-condition-inline): cannot inline the call to `readFlag`
  used as an `assert` condition in a constructor
```

Both previously produced compiling output. Diagnostics are located and
name the offending circuit or native.

**Honest gap:** I could not construct a probe reaching the `if` case.
Every shape tried was handled earlier — the constructor folds ledger
reads against the known initial state, and a witness-valued condition is
rejected by disclosure analysis first. It is the identical code shape as
the assert case and is now guarded, but treat it as cheap insurance
rather than a fix for a demonstrated bug.

## The documentation half

8 of 9 pass files had no file-level comment — straight from the licence
block into a helper definition. All 9 now state what they own.

**A correction that changed this commit's shape:** the audit claimed
there was no module map. There was — `compiler/README-rust-passes.md`,
which I missed by only looking in `doc/` and `docs/`. I had written a
separate architecture doc, found the existing one, and **deleted mine**,
folding the material in. Two maps would diverge, and next to the code is
where a compiler engineer looks.

The README gained the three things a first-time reader actually needs:

- **the walker/emit split and its cost** — both layers must understand
the same IR shapes, so a new construct usually needs handling in *both*;
emitter-without-walker is silently unsupported, walker-without-emitter
is a crash
- **the three body routes** (constructor / impure / pure) and why they
differ
- **what each test layer can and cannot catch** — byte-parity locks the
*text*, executing tests lock the *meaning*: a wrong lowering that
happens to serialise identically passes byte-parity, and a correct
lowering that is merely reformatted fails it

It also had a convention that was actively misleading — *"walkers bail
to `unimplemented!()` rather than producing wrong code"* — which is the
same mistake this PR removes. Plus stale facts: "seven Scheme files"
(nine), every LOC figure, and a missing row for `rust-passes-naming.ss`.

`docs/rust-backend-limitations.md` now exists on this branch. It was
written on the ledger-9 line and never existed here — on the branch the
CoIP cites as the reference implementation. Counts verified for *this*
branch: 28 rejection sites, 24 kinds.

Dangling `docs/superpowers/**` pointers removed from everything that
ships: that directory is a dated internal journal that will not exist
upstream, and three of the links were in `runtime-rs` /
`runtime-rs-macros`, so they would have shipped as broken links in
published rustdoc.

## What I found but did not fix

`rendered-has-todo?` is a string-sniffing net that body emitters use to
bail when a sub-render produced a placeholder — and **it is why the
corpus is clean.** Real, working defence-in-depth. But it, and the ~31
remaining `(guard (c [#t #f]) …)` probes, share one root cause:
**unsupported-ness is not representable as a type**, so a deliberate
rejection and a genuine bug raise indistinguishable conditions. Filed as
**#41** rather than fixed, since it is a design change that will surface
currently-masked bugs and deserves its own diff.

8018e02a1bd7cd35215f0b6ac6cadf56971ee27b.message:
Fixes #5 (compiler gap **G1**).

## The bug

A pure circuit whose assert subtracted a struct-field projection failed
to compile:

```compact
struct Inner2 { createdAt: Uint<64>; }
struct Pol { enforce: Boolean; maxAge: Uint<64>; }
export pure circuit oneLevel(p: Pol, a2: Inner2, now: Uint<64>): [] {
  if (p.enforce) {
    assert(now - a2.createdAt <= p.maxAge, "too old");
  }
}
```

```
Exception: repro.compact line 5 char 1:
  compactc --rust: unsupported Compact construct (pure-circuit-body-emission): no walker shape
  matched pure circuit body for oneLevel
```

## Root cause

The `if` guard turned out to be **incidental** — the same assert without
the guard failed identically. The real trigger is a struct-field
projection as an operand of *trapping* arithmetic.

The typer wraps trapping unsigned arithmetic in an underflow guard `(seq
(assert (>= a b)) (- a b))` and let\*-lifts any operand that isn't
already a simple local into its own temp. A projection is such an
operand, so the lowering nests **two** levels of lifted assignment:

```scheme
(= %t.6 (seq (= %t.7 (elt-ref a2 createdAt 0))
             (seq (assert (>= %now %t.7) "result of subtraction would be negative")
                  (- 64 %now %t.7))))
```

`stmt-flatten`'s `lift-seq-prefix-exprs` hoists the **outer** level to a
statement, where `stmt-pure-body-rust`'s `stmt->assignment` clause
lowers it as `let <temp> = <rhs>;`. The **inner** level stayed inside
the RHS and reached `seq-stmt-rust`
(`compiler/rust-passes-emit.ss:1691`), which handled only `assert` and
fell through to `expr-rust` — which has no `(=)` clause at all, so the
body bailed.

That is exactly the asymmetry the issue predicted: the seq-block
renderer was a restricted subset of the statement renderer. Plain scalar
operands need only one level, and the same projection under `==` rather
than `<=` also stays single-level — which is why every ingredient
compiled in isolation.

## Fix

Unified on the statement renderer's machinery rather than adding a
second projection-aware path:

- `seq-stmt-rust` gained a `(= ,src ,var-name ,expr)` clause that
renders through the **same** helpers as `stmt-pure-body-rust`'s
`stmt->assignment` clause — `uniquify-rust-name` over
`current-var-substitution`, then `expr-rust` for the RHS. Projections
still lower through the single existing `elt-ref` clause in `expr-rust`.
- `expr-rust`'s `seq` clause now **folds** its prefix statements instead
of mapping them, so a binding one introduces is in scope for the
statements after it and for the tail — the same left-to-right
substitution threading the statement level already does.
- The two `let`-binding clauses in `stmt-pure-body-rust` reserve their
own Rust name for the duration of the RHS render, so a temp lifted from
inside it uniquifies (`t_0`) instead of shadowing the binder.

Generated output for the repro:

```rust
pub fn one_level(p: Pol, a2: Inner2, now: u64) -> Result<(), CompactError> {
    Ok(if p.enforce {
        let t = {
            let t_0 = a2.createdAt;
            {
                compact_assert!((now >= t_0), "result of subtraction would be negative");
                ((now) as u64).wrapping_sub((t_0) as u64)
            }
        };
        compact_assert!((t <= p.maxAge), "too old");
    })
}
```

New fixture `examples/guarded_assert_arith_fixture.compact` (nested
`attestation.proof.createdAt` projection, both `-` and `<=`, guarded and

Plus an executing gate,

each assert, because byte parity alone cannot distinguish a correct

- `guarded_max_age_assert_passes_at_the_boundary` — inclusive `<=`

- `guarded_max_age_assert_trips_when_too_old` — pins the subtraction

- `subtraction_underflow_is_trapped_not_wrapped` — a dropped guard would
wrap on `u64` and silently pass
- `two_projection_operands_compute_the_real_difference` — asserts the
returned difference is 100, proving the two lifted temps stayed distinct
- `impure_caller_propagates_the_guarded_assert_failure` —
`?`-propagation out of the impure caller, plus the success path

848c36e0e873a44f617172988b811cec5b84f2fe.message:
`vminstr->builder-call`'s `idx` op handler hardcoded
`(= (length indices) 1)` and returned #f for any path with more than
one element. This broke the OpProgramVerify chain for write/update
ops whose ledger fields live under a nested ledger struct — A8
already did the same fix for `vminstr->gather-builder-call`
(OpProgramGather, used by read ops); this is the same change for
the Verify pipeline.

Concrete trigger: did.compact's `recordUpdate` body emits

  operationCount.increment  at path (1 6)
  version.increment         at path (1 1)
  updated                 = at path (1 3)

(the leading `1` is the wrapper around the schnorr-prefixed import's
ledger struct). The A10 walker changes correctly routed all three
through the pl-call mutation tag, but pl-call-builder-lines bottomed
out at vminstr->builder-call's idx handler returning #f for the
2-element path, so emit-body-mutations returned #f and the dispatcher
reported "no walker shape matched" despite body-walkable? having
accepted the body.

Fix mirrors A8: drop the length-1 branch and emit one
`.idx_at_index(N, push)` per index using the same per-element loop.
n=1 is now just the specialisation; n>1 produces the chain that
expand-vm-code intended.

did.compact's recordUpdate + rotateControllerKey now compile end to
end (next gap surfaces at setAlsoKnownAs, a separate if/else-if
shape — tracked as A12). 24 codegen_regression fixtures still pass.

8c0ec1646ed7e6a445eea1d1875d2c3cae424a15.message:
Closes the last did.compact downstream error by short-circuiting the
unimpleable `schnorrVerify<#n>` generic-circuit emission with an
orphan-safe Rust helper that reuses the off-circuit verifier already
shipped in midnight-ledger's `transient_crypto::schnorr`.

Runtime (`runtime-rs/src/std_lib/schnorr.rs`):
  - Vendor the ~50 LOC off-circuit Schnorr verifier (pinned
    `midnight-transient-crypto 2.1.0` doesn't yet expose its own
    `schnorr` module; the impl was added post-2.1.0). Algorithm matches
    `jubjub-schnorr/src/schnorr.compact`'s `schnorrVerify` exactly:
    Poseidon over [ann_x, ann_y, pk_x, pk_y, ...msg], reduce mod the
    Jubjub scalar order, check g^s == announcement + pk^c. The Compact
    side uses `getSchnorrReduction` to expose the reduction as a
    circuit-friendly (q, r) pair; off-circuit we just take the modular
    reduction directly via `embedded::Scalar::from_bytes_wide`.
  - `pub struct SchnorrSignature { announcement: JubjubPoint, response:
    EmbeddedFr }` — layout matches the Compact-side struct so codegen
    field-by-field conversions line up.
  - Circuit-shaped wrapper `schnorr_verify_jubjub<PS, const N: usize>(
    ctx, msg, sig, pk) -> Result<CircuitResults<PS, ()>, CompactError>`
    that asserts on rejection and threads ctx through a no-op
    query_for_verify, returning a CircuitResults shape identical to
    what an inlined Compact assert body would produce.
  - Re-exports at crate root and `std_lib::`.

Codegen (`compiler/rust-passes-helpers.ss` + 6 emit sites in
`rust-passes-walker.ss` + `rust-passes-streaming.ss`):
  - New `impure-call-target` helper returns either `self.<cname>` (the
    default) or a `compact_runtime::*` override path. Currently the
    only override is `schnorr_verify` → `compact_runtime::schnorr_verify_jubjub`.
  - All six `self.~a(ctx, ...)?` emit sites for impure-circuit calls
    now route through the helper.

Net effect: did.compact's generated lib.rs goes from 1 unique
remaining cargo check error to 0 once midnight-did-rs's flake pin is
refreshed. All 28 tests-e2e-rust byte-parity fixtures still pass.

When upstream `midnight-transient-crypto` exposes `schnorr` in a future
release, the vendored bits in `std_lib/schnorr.rs` can be deleted in
favour of `pub use midnight_transient_crypto::schnorr::*` and the
wrapper unchanged.

8c34586b5adb68446de0194efa7cb47780e5fd1a.message:
Accepts @patextreme's second point from the review of
LFDT-Minokawa/compact#730: the crate should be
`midnight-compact-runtime`, not `compact-runtime`.

```
compact-runtime         → midnight-compact-runtime
compact-runtime-macros  → midnight-compact-runtime-macros
compact_runtime         → midnight_compact_runtime
compact_runtime_macros  → midnight_compact_runtime_macros
```

Midnight's Rust crates are uniformly `midnight-*`; the prefix does for
Rust what the `@midnight-ntwrk` scope does for npm, and
`compact-runtime` alone is generic on crates.io. Generated code names
the crate in **every `use`**, so it is effectively permanent once
anything is published — cheap now, expensive later. The crate is
unpublished, so no consumer is affected and the **runtime version is
unchanged** (0.16.100).

## The hazard, and how it was handled

The **TypeScript** runtime is also called `compact-runtime`
(`@midnight-ntwrk/compact-runtime`). Renaming that would break the TS
backend, so the two spellings were treated differently:

- **snake_case `compact_runtime`** — unambiguously a Rust path.
Rewritten everywhere.
- **kebab-case `compact-runtime`** — ambiguous. Rewritten only in files
where it denotes the Rust crate, and never after `@midnight-ntwrk/`.

Verified preserved: `compiler/midnight-ledger.ss` keeps its 10 TS
references, `compiler/test.ss` its TS import, and the two `Cargo.toml`
descriptions that mention the npm package. Directory names `runtime-rs/`
and `runtime-rs-macros/` are unchanged. Dated design records under
`docs/superpowers/**` are left as written — they are history, not live
docs.

## Fixture churn

All 32 byte-parity fixtures regenerated. Diffs are the new paths **plus
rustfmt reflow**: `midnight_compact_runtime` is 9 characters longer,
pushing some lines past the 100-column limit. Classified every hunk
before regenerating — no semantic changes.

`digital-passport` has no committed `.compact` source, so it is not
regenerable; it was renamed textually and reformatted. That is exactly
the fmt-only gating AGENT.md §3.3 describes.

## One thing worth flagging

The first pass **missed `compiler/snapshots/*.txt`** — the emitter's own
`print-rust` goldens — because the rename script's suffix list had no
`.txt`. Every Rust-side gate passed anyway: fmt, clippy, `cargo test`,
and byte-parity. Only **`./compiler/go` caught it** (`print-rust 0/1`).

That is the second time in this batch that `./compiler/go` caught
something all four Rust gates were blind to. The script now covers
`.txt` and `.compact`.

## Verification

fmt clean · clippy `-D warnings` clean · byte-parity green against the
regenerated corpus · **`./compiler/go` exit 0, zero failures, both
`print-rust` snapshots passing**.

## Merge ordering

This touches ~140 files including every fixture, so it will conflict
with any open PR that moves fixture bytes. Recommended order: land #19,
#20, #24, #25 first, then these two renames. The rename is fully
scripted, so re-applying after a rebase is mechanical rather than
manual.

Companion PR for the ledger-9 line renames the same crate there, so
generated code stays consistent across both.

9e32ce7415949b19c692d8a9f00f6fc6ef8c7fae.message:
Review findings from patextreme on #19.

1. Widening-cast coverage (blocking) — the finding is CORRECT that
   coverage was lost, but its diagnosis needs one precise correction: the
   widening sub-case is NOT untested. map_lambda_fixture's `x * 2` on
   Uint<64> has mbits=65, so it emits `((x) as u128).wrapping_mul(...)`
   from u64 operands — a genuine widening. The real gap is narrower and
   still worth closing: of the five rungs in `mbits->rust-width`, only
   u64 (same-width no-op) and u128 (widening) were reached. u8/u16/u32
   and BOTH interior boundaries were unexercised, and the deleted
   digital-passport was the sole carrier of the u32 rung.

   That matters because a wrong rung cannot fault. `wrapping_*` truncates
   silently, so an off-by-one in a `(<= mbits N)` comparison yields a
   WRONG VALUE in generated code that still compiles and still passes
   byte-parity, since byte-parity only pins the text.

   Added examples/widening_arith_fixture.compact — four pure circuits
   covering u16 and u32 from both u8 and u16 operands, including the
   `Uint<8> * 365` shape the emitter's own comment cites:

     sum_bytes(255,255)        mbits=9  -> u16   510  (u8 rung: 254)
     age_threshold_days(255)   mbits=17 -> u32 93075  (u16 rung: 27539)
     product_bytes(255,255)    mbits=16 -> u16 65025  (u8 rung: 1)
     area_of(65535,65535)      mbits=32 -> u32   4294836225 (u16: 1)

   Each is registered in FIXTURES for byte-parity AND has an executing
   test asserting the value, because byte-parity alone cannot tell
   `as u32` from `as u16`. The parenthesised values are what a
   one-rung-too-narrow cast would silently produce.

2. Duplicated block reader (minor) — extracted to tests/common/mod.rs as
   `generated_fn_body`. Note only ONE copy remained: the duplicate died
   with did05_constructor_readback.rs, so this is about naming the
   operation and being ready for the next paste, not removing live
   duplication. It panics rather than returning Option, so a caller
   cannot assert vacuously against a body it failed to find.

3. Comment traceability (minor) — A-05 is NOT decommissioned. It is
   covered twice: schnorr_attest_fixture (JubjubPoint ledger read
   forwarded into the verifier) and asset_registry_fixture (ledger read
   into an impure call from a constructor, so the hoist coexists with the
   A28 write-flush). Both emit `_carg_` temps. Added fixture pointers at
   hoist-ctx-args and at mbits->rust-width naming the neutral fixtures,
   which restores traceability without reintroducing branding.

4. Out-of-scope doc scrub — treated differently by kind, deliberately:
   - docs/adr/0001 Follow-ups claimed digital-passport "is not yet
     registered in codegen_regression". That is a LIVE follow-up that can
     no longer be actioned, so it is now marked closed-by-removal.
     Verified the replacement claim: 34 contract dirs, 34 FIXTURES
     entries, zero ungated.
   - CHANGELOG.md references are left ALONE. Those entries record work
     that genuinely happened against fixtures that existed at the time;
     rewriting them would falsify the record, and they do not ship
     upstream anyway — the curated series carries a fresh entry in
     upstream's format (see #22).

a45d68d1acddeb8574ceccf943ddaa8af9d15909.message:
Closes the third codegen bug surfaced by the codegen_regression
mass-regen sweep. After A18+A19 (commit f9b509f) extended the impure
body-shape dispatcher to emit non-exported impure helpers as inherent
methods on Contract<PS, W>, tiny.compact's `circuit in_state(s: STATE):
Boolean` lands as a `pub(crate) fn in_state(..., s: STATE)`. But the
type-declarations pass never learned to walk that new reachability path,
so the `STATE` enum (declared in tiny but not exported and not used as a
ledger field type — `STATE` IS used in the ledger but that path was
already covered by E2) was the wrong example. Concretely, the regen
emitted:

    pub(crate) fn in_state(&self, ..., s: STATE) -> ...

with no top-level `STATE` decl, and rustc rejected the generated lib.rs:

    error[E0425]: cannot find type `STATE` in this scope

The decl walker only promoted user types reached via two paths:
  (1) the `export { ... }` block (analysis-passes E2 walker), or
  (2) ledger field types (publicly-reachable surface).

A18+A19 introduced a third reachability path — types referenced by the
sigs of emitted non-exported impure circuits — that neither walker
followed.

This mirrors the M3.5-E4.4 Blocker 2 fix for pure circuits
(commit history #22, "promote ledger-referenced & sig-referenced user
structs to export-typedef"): we already had
`collect-pure-circuit-tdefns` for the non-exported *pure* circuit case
(zerocash's `derive_nullifier(...): nullifier`). The fix extends the
same scan to non-exported impure circuits whose bodies are walkable per
`impure-circuit-body-walkable?` — exactly the set that gets emitted as
methods downstream. Build the native/witness/circuit id htables once at
the top of the Program pass and thread them to both the decl-collector
and the impure-emit site (the htables were previously rebuilt inside
the parameterize block; now they're hoisted to the outer let*).

Net effect on tiny.compact: lib.rs now includes the `pub enum STATE`
decl + impls (Aligned / FieldRepr / FromFieldRepr / From<STATE> for
Value / BinaryHashRepr) alongside the `in_state` inherent method, and
the generated crate compiles cleanly.

a529597113b4ae31e6973bb7d2304c22c2f5ddc2.message:
Two CI-correctness fixes for the stable branch. Both are cases where a
gate looked green while guaranteeing nothing.

## 1. The ledger line is now enforced, not remembered

The fork carries two ledger lines simultaneously:

| Branch | Ledger | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `codegen-rust` (stable) | **8** | published crates.io versions
(`midnight-zswap = "8"`, `midnight-onchain-* = "3"`) |
| `develop` (forward) | **9** | git tags on
`midnightntwrk/midnight-ledger` (`ledger-9.x`) |

That split has held so far purely by convention. It is a weak guarantee
for the failure it guards against: a ledger-9 pin merged into
`codegen-rust` would make the branch **the CoIP cites as the reference
implementation** depend on an unreleased ledger, and *no existing gate
would notice* — the Rust tests pass on either line, so CI would be green
and the breakage would only surface for someone building against
released crates.

`ledger-line-check.yml` derives the expected line from the PR's base
branch. Verified against every real manifest in the repo:

| Head → base | Result |
|---|---|
| `codegen-rust` → `codegen-rust` | PASS (ledger 8, published) |
| `neutral-fixtures` (#19) → `codegen-rust` | PASS (ledger 8, published)
|
| `integrate-upstream-0.33` (#20) → `develop` | PASS (ledger 9, git
tags) |
| **`integrate-upstream-0.33` (#20) → `codegen-rust`** | **FAIL — ledger
9 pins blocked** |
| `develop` → `develop` | PASS (no pins yet, still ledger 8) |
| `main` → `main` | SKIP (mirrors upstream) |

Row 4 is the whole point. Note `develop` deliberately passes while it
carries no ledger git pins, so the gate does not fire before #20 lands.

Only `[workspace.dependencies]` `ledger-` tags count;
`[patch.crates-io]` carries unrelated tags like
`transient-crypto-2.2.0-rc.1`.

**No branch restructuring is needed** — `codegen-rust`/`develop` already
*are* the ledger-8/ledger-9 pair. Adding separate `ledger8`/`ledger9`
branches would duplicate them and leave four long-lived branches to keep
in sync. What was missing was enforcement and legibility, which is what
this adds.

## 2. The byte-parity gate has never run in CI

`rust_codegen_byte_parity_against_committed_fixtures` regenerates every
fixture with `compactc --rust` and asserts byte-identity — our strongest
emitter-correctness signal. The `Test` jobs are bare runners with no
`nix build`, so `./result/bin/compactc` is absent, and the test detected
that and returned `Ok` after printing `SKIP`.

So CI has been reporting a green byte-parity gate that regenerated
nothing for the entire life of this branch — **including on #19, the PR
that swaps the whole fixture corpus**, where it matters most. (#19's
fixtures were verified locally; CI simply did not check them.)

Two commits here:

- **`d21b2b6`** makes the missing-compiler path fail instead of skip.
- **`3e0c70a`** updates the only CI caller: the bare-runner job excludes
that one test **by name** (`-- --skip rust_codegen_byte_parity`) rather
than restoring an in-test escape hatch. The distinction matters — the
test keeps no skip path of its own, so any run that executes it is
guaranteed to have had a real compiler, and the exclusion is visible in
the workflow step and in libtest's `filtered out` count instead of
buried in test logic. Everything else in `tests-e2e-rust` still gates;
`codegen_regression.rs` holds only this one test.

Making the gate genuinely run in CI needs a compactc on the runner —
tracked in #23 (preferred approach: share the binary
`build-compiler.yml` already builds, rather than paying for a second nix
build).

## Verification

- Guard logic exercised against all six head/base combinations above.
- Workflow YAML parses; embedded script passes `bash -n` and runs
correctly.
- `cargo test -p tests-e2e-rust --locked -- --skip
rust_codegen_byte_parity` green locally (the exact CI invocation).
- The hard-failure direction is confirmed by CI itself: it is what
turned #20's `Test` jobs red.

Labeled `skip-changelog` — CI-only, no compiler behavior change, so no
`CHANGELOG.md`/`compiler-version.ss` bump.

Related: #22 (upstream hygiene — this workflow is fork-local and must
not go upstream), #23.

a55a651e45659f05e4b5740cb9fd9593906d8997.message:
Adopts patextreme's first interface point on LFDT-Minokawa/compact#730
(closes MediaNoxLabs/compact#30).

My earlier objection — that `--rust` + `--skip-ts` preserves backward
compatibility — rested on a premise that does not hold: neither flag
exists upstream, so there are no invocations to preserve. With `ts`
implied when the flag is absent, today's command lines are untouched
under either design. The real difference is forward compatibility:
`--skip-ts` becomes ambiguous the moment a third backend lands, forcing
exactly the breaking rename `--target` avoids.

  compactc c.compact out/                          -> TS   (implied)
  compactc --target rust c.compact out/            -> Rust only
  compactc --target rust --target ts c.compact out/ -> both

The list REPLACES the default rather than adding to it, which is what
lets `--target rust` subsume `--rust --skip-ts` with no flag-combination
validation, while keeping "emit both" expressible for the parity harness.
`--skip-zk` stays orthogonal.

Implementation. third_party/compiler/command-line-parsing.ss keeps only
the LAST value of a repeated flag — "the final value of each
corresponding <var> is its last specified value" — so a plain value clause
would have turned `--target rust --target ts` into just `ts`. Silently
wrong is worse than unsupported, so accumulation uses the grammar's
per-occurrence `$ <action>` hook instead, leaving the vendored parser
untouched.

Validation runs in the matched clause body, NOT in the action: actions can
fire while a clause is only being attempted, so erroring inside one could
reject a --target value on a command line that never matched that clause.
Collection is deduped, which also makes a repeated fire for a single
occurrence harmless.

`--rust` / `--skip-ts` keep working as undocumented aliases so this fork's
harness and MediaNoxLabs/midnight-identity (which invokes
`compactc --rust --skip-ts`) do not break in the same change. Mixing
`--target` with either alias is an error rather than a silent precedence
rule, so no invocation can be read two ways. The aliases are
fork-transitional — upstream never shipped the flags, so there is nothing
to deprecate there and they must not be carried upstream (#22).

The byte-parity gate now invokes `--target rust`, so CI exercises the new
flag. A parsing regression would surface there as every fixture drifting
(no lib.rs emitted at all) rather than as a flag bug; the test comment
says so, since that failure mode reads like a codegen catastrophe.

Verified against the built binary rather than assumed — the accumulation
behaviour was the part the parser docs made uncertain:

  (no flag)                    rc=0  ts=YES rust=no
  --target ts                  rc=0  ts=YES rust=no
  --target rust                rc=0  ts=no  rust=YES
  --target rust --target ts    rc=0  ts=YES rust=YES
  --target ts --target rust    rc=0  ts=YES rust=YES   (order-independent)
  --rust --skip-ts (alias)     rc=0  ts=no  rust=YES
  --rust (alias)               rc=0  ts=YES rust=YES
  --target go                  rc=1  unknown --target "go"; valid targets are ts, rust
  --target rust --target go    rc=1  (rejected even when one value is valid)
  --target rust --rust         rc=1  --target cannot be combined with --rust or --skip-ts
  --target ts --skip-ts        rc=1  (same)
  --skip-ts alone              rc=255 pre-existing "--skip-ts requires --rust" check intact

Gates: fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean, 48 test groups pass,
byte-parity green THROUGH `--target rust` (so the new flag provably emits
byte-identical output to the old one), ./compiler/go exit 0 with zero
failures and both print-rust snapshots passing, and tests-e2e 50 files /
492 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed.

Compiler version 0.31.112 -> 0.31.113 with a versioned CHANGELOG heading.
Migrated invocations and live docs; historical records under
docs/superpowers/** keep the flags they were written with.

a763a7c1fddd7d904d0da3bc24e76d1aa353337d.message:
Closes did.compact's setAlsoKnownAs end-to-end and fixes a latent
A12 correctness bug (the Remove arm was silently dropped). Now
unblocks setVerificationMethod (next gap, A14).

THREE small additions:

1. Ltypescript Statement has BOTH a 3-arg `(if cond stmt1 stmt2)`
   form AND a 2-arg `(if cond stmt1)` no-else form (langs.ss:875).
   stmt->public-ledger-write detected only the 3-arg variant, so
   `else if (...)` chains with no terminal else surfaced as a 2-arg
   if whose A12 dispatch missed the else-if peel. Extend
   `stmt->if-then-else` (rust-passes-walker.ss:2237) to admit the
   2-arg form, synthesising a `(statement-expression (tuple src))`
   no-op else so downstream code sees a uniform 3-element shape.

   Concrete impact: did.compact's setAlsoKnownAs body is

     if (mutation == Insert) { … }
     else if (mutation == Remove) { … }

   where the inner Remove-branch if has no source else. Before A13,
   stmt->if-then-else returned #f on the inner if, so loop-arms in
   the A12 emit dispatch only saw the Insert arm and emitted a
   single-arm if/else with the Remove case silently dropped. With
   the 2-arg form supported, loop-arms now peels the Remove arm
   correctly.

2. `Op::Rem { cached }` exists in midnight-onchain-vm's ops (Set/Map
   remove vm-code) but had no builder method or codegen support.
   Adds:
   - `OpProgramVerify::rem(cached: bool)` builder method in
     runtime-rs/src/op_builder.rs.
   - `"rem"` case in `vminstr->builder-call` (rust-passes-emit.ss:843)
     rendering `.rem(<cached>)`.

   The compiler's vm-code for Set.remove ends with
   `(idx)(push)(rem)(ins)`; without the rem handler, vminstr->builder-call
   returned #f for that op and compute-pl-builder-lines bailed, which
   in the A12 emit cascade produced arm-info=#f for the Remove arm.

gap at line 246, setVerificationMethod, tracked as A14).

The setVerificationMethod shape (in-branch lifted-let + assign +
assert + Map.insert with struct value + unconditional post-if
pl-call) is structurally bigger and tracked separately.

ad6028fbfa9c6c38d3dd07ada7d82d232a15ea93.message:
R1 walker gap A7 closure. Pre-fix, emit-body-or-fallback's
(null? stmts) tail returned #f when `writes` (the tagged
mutations accumulator) was empty — leaving assert-only bodies
without an OpProgramVerify chain to anchor, which the dispatcher
treated as "no walker shape matched".

did.compact's `assertController()` body is a single assert with
no state mutation; the prior session's A6 fix unblocked the
witness-inline issue, but the body itself fell through to this
emit-time failure.

The minimal fix: let assert-only bodies (writes empty, but
pre-lines non-empty) flow through emit-body-mutations with an
empty mutations list. The function emits an empty
OpProgramVerify chain — query_for_verify on a `.build()`-only
chain succeeds and threads ctx through unchanged, which is
exactly the correct "side-effect-free" semantics for an assert.

Bodies with absolutely no pre-lines AND no writes (an empty
function body) still return #f — there's literally nothing for
the walker to emit. They fall through to the streaming walker /
error path per the existing chain.

Non-regression: tests-e2e-rust codegen_regression test still
passes — all 24 byte-parity fixtures emit byte-identically. No
existing fixture has an assert-only body that previously fell
through to #f, so the new path doesn't change any committed
lib.rs.

did.compact progress: assertController and assertControllerCanUpdate
bodies now emit. compactc proceeds further and surfaces the next
gap: `adt-read-with-arg-lowering` (likely Map.lookup or similar
read-with-args ADT op in another did.compact circuit). Tracked
as A8.

afec3cf75a9a6eff717a275cb3820cbf0bc60c27.message:
Promotes the integration branch to stable. Two compiler/runtime fixes,
each merged to `develop` with full CI green and each carrying an
**executing** regression test (not just byte-parity):

### A30 — alignment-aware `decode_via_field_repr` (#10, toolchain
0.31.110)
Ledger-read decoding converted AlignedValue atoms → Frs **1:1**, but
cells are *alignment*-encoded (one atom per leaf, a leaf worth multiple
field-repr Frs). Consequences: `ledger().id()` (`Bytes<32>` = 1 atom vs
`FIELD_SIZE` 2) could **never** decode, and struct map-value lookups
mis-sliced. Now walks `av.alignment` in lockstep — `Bytes{len}` →
`ceil(len/31)` Frs in the upstream `[u8]` layout, empty atom → zero Frs.
- Gate: the did-05 executing constructor readback (left `#[ignore]`d by
#4) is **un-ignored and asserts `ledger().id()`**.
- Known residual, fails loudly rather than silently: non-empty string
leaves inside structs (generated `from_field_repr` allots them 0 Fr
slots) — needs variable-size-aware slicing in codegen.

### G1 — struct-field projection in trapping-arithmetic operands (#12,
toolchain 0.31.111)
Filed as a "guarded assert" bug; the guard turned out to be
**incidental** (verified: the unguarded form fails identically on this
branch's base). Real trigger: a projection as an operand of *trapping*
arithmetic, which the typer expands to nested lifted assignments — the
inner one reached `seq-stmt-rust`, which had no `(=)` clause. Fixed by
routing it through the **same** `stmt->assignment` helpers as the
statement renderer (no second projection path — deliberately avoiding
the duplicated-path mode that caused A29).
- Unblocks `revocation-registry.compact` and
`secret-birth-credential.compact` upstream (VC coverage 11/18 → 13/18),
including the last blocker for the VC core crates.

### Parity
Both changes: **zero fixture drift, no re-blessing** (did-05 included).
A30 is runtime-only; G1 affects only a shape no existing fixture uses.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

b08f71a89f9e947c4a9954bd7ffe55bf7762765e.message:
Regression coverage for the Bug-11 codegen fix (commit f766a4b).
The fixture exercises three sequential write circuits whose
destination fields span the three relevant cases:

  * tiny   : Uint<0..100>           — byte_len=1 (matches Rust u8)
  * medium : Uint<0..70000>         — byte_len=3 (non-power-of-2, u32)
  * wide   : Uint<0..5_000_000_000> — byte_len=5 (non-power-of-2, u64)

The medium and wide writes are the previously-broken case: pre-Bug-11
the codegen emitted `new_cell(v)` (4- or 8-byte Rust width descriptor)
instead of `new_cell_bounded_uint(v as u128, byte_len)` (TS's
3- or 5-byte on-state descriptor), producing wrong serialised bytes.

The byte-parity test (bug11_fixture.rs) drives initial_state →
set_tiny → set_medium → set_wide and asserts the serialised
ContractState matches the TS reference at every step. The TS
reference is produced by tests-e2e-rust/fixtures/capture-bug11-fixture.mjs
(mirroring the set-size capture pattern, post-A20 idiom).

The fixture is also registered in codegen_regression's FIXTURES list
so future Scheme-side drift surfaces as a regen mismatch.

canonical missing shape:

  circuit recordUpdate(): [] {
    operationCount.increment(1);            // non-write PL call
    version.increment(1);                    // non-write PL call
    updated = disclose(currentTimestamp());  // Cell.write
  }

Implementation (Path A from the gap analysis):

- rust-passes-walker.ss body-walkable?: new clause accepting non-write
  public-ledger calls in non-terminal position (single-index path,
  supported arg exprs — mirroring the existing terminal-PL-call
  predicate). The earlier terminal clause keeps its `(null? writes)`
  guard so counter.compact's sole-stmt body remains byte-stable.

- rust-passes-walker.ss emit-body-or-fallback: parallel clause for
  emit. The `writes` accumulator now carries tagged entries — either
  ('cell-write idx . expr) for Cell.write or ('pl-call src adt-op
  path-elt* expr*) for a non-write PL call — preserving source order.
  emit-body-mutations replaces emit-body-writes and dispatches per
  tag, splicing per-entry builder lines into a single OpProgramVerify
  chain. Return value now properly propagates: emit-body-or-fallback
  returns whatever emit-body-mutations returns rather than always #t,
  so a failed lowering surfaces as the expected hard codegen error
  rather than a silently incomplete body.

- pl-call-builder-lines (new helper): shared lowering of a non-write
  PL call into builder-call lines via expand-vm-code +
  vminstr->builder-call. Extracted from
  emit-non-write-public-ledger-terminal's inner pipeline so both the
  terminal-only and the mutations-chain paths share rendering.

- rust-passes-emit.ss vminstr->builder-call (`addi` case): extended
  to accept vm-rust-expr immediates (the wrapped Rust expression
  string produced when an integer literal arg lowers through a
  const-binding gensym, per Prod-14). Emits `.addi(<expr> as u32)`
  matching the runtime addi parameter width

b871ec5909c7655deca1b5a362da3ef802d81b0a.message:
Closes did.compact's setAlsoKnownAs (and the structurally identical
setVerificationMethodRelation, insertVerificationMethodRelation,
removeVerificationMethodRelationFromLedger). Body shape:

  assertControllerCanUpdate();
  const disclosedMutation = disclose(mutation);
  assertSetMutationDefined(disclosedMutation);
  const alias = disclose(value);
  if (disclosedMutation == SetMutation.Insert) {
    assert(!alsoKnownAs.member(alias), "...");
    alsoKnownAs.insert(alias);
  } else if (disclosedMutation == SetMutation.Remove) {
    assert(alsoKnownAs.member(alias), "...");
    alsoKnownAs.remove(alias);
  }
  recordUpdate();

Three structural challenges:
(a) Each branch is `(seq (assert ...) (pl-call ...))` — multi-stmt.
(b) The else-branch is itself an if-then-else (else-if pattern).
(c) The inner if has no source else — the IR puts `(tuple #f)` in
    the else slot.

Changes:

1. New helper `branch->assert-and-pl-call` (rust-passes-walker.ss
   after line 2505) as sibling to `branch->single-pl-call`. Admits
   one optional leading `(assert ...)` before the terminal pl-call,
   chasing const-bindings through `expr-resolve`. Returns
   `(list assert-opt src adt-op path-elt* resolved-expr*)`.

2. `body-streaming-walkable?` if-then-else clause
   (rust-passes-streaming.ss:117) extended to admit the A12 shape:
   either branch matches the legacy single-pl-call OR the new
   assert+pl-call. Walks the else-if chain recursively; accepts a
   `(tuple #f)`-shaped no-else terminator.

3. New A12 emit clause in `emit-streaming-body`
   (rust-passes-streaming.ss:524) — runs BEFORE the legacy E6.2
   clause with a guard that defers to E6.2 when both branches are
   E6.2-shaped (single-pl-call, no assert). For the A12 shape:
   pre-walks the if-tree into a list of `(cond-expr arm-info)` pairs
   plus optional final else; emits one Rust `if cond1 { ... } else
   if cond2 { ... } else { ... };` chain where each branch lays its
   own `compact_assert!(...)` then a per-arm OpProgramVerify chain
   feeding `query_for_verify`. Missing else emits an empty
   `OpProgramVerify::new().build()` no-op so __gas_acc and ctx
   threading stay uniform across all paths.

4. After the if/else-if chain, A12 emits
   `let ctx = CircuitContext { current_query_context: _if_results_N.context, ..ctx };`
   so subsequent statements (e.g. `recordUpdate()` in setAlsoKnownAs)
   see the updated context through the default `&ctx.current_query_context`
   ctx-expr — no need to extend the impure-exported bare-call handler
   to accept non-default ctx-expr.

Non-regressive: 24 codegen_regression fixtures byte-stable
(if_stmt_fixture, election vote$commit/$reveal, zerocash.spend all
route through the unchanged legacy E6.2 clause; A12 guard defers
when both branches are single-pl-call).

ba971d513218483fbcfe3a24be34d6c69141a9b4.message:
Fixes #85

## Root cause

On darwin, nixpkgs deliberately pairs **every** LLVM set's clang wrapper
with the **top-level `darwin.libcxx`** (the "system libc++"), not the
set's own libc++ — see `systemLibcxxClang` /
`clangWithLibcAndBasicRtAndLibcxx` in
`pkgs/development/compilers/llvm/common/default.nix`.

Our `chez` override pinned `stdenv = pkgs.llvmPackages_18.stdenv`, so
after the nixpkgs bump in #69:

| aarch64-darwin | old pin `bcc4a9d9` | new pin `c27cdad4` |
|---|---|---|
| `llvmPackages_18.stdenv.cc.cc` | clang 18.1.8 | clang 18.1.8 |
| `llvmPackages_18.stdenv.cc.libcxx` | **libcxx-20.1.0**+apple-sdk-26.0
| **libcxx-21.1.6**+apple-sdk-26.5 |

libc++ 21 headers use `__builtin_ctzg` unconditionally (a clang ≥ 19
builtin), so `compiler-rt-libc-18.1.8` — which nixpkgs *always* builds
against `darwin.libcxx` — fails to compile with clang-18, cascading to
`clang-wrapper-18.1.8` → `stdenv-darwin` → `chez-scheme-10.4.1` →
`compactc`.

## Why this fix

- **Drop the pin** (option 2 from the issue): nixpkgs itself builds
`chez-scheme-10.4.1` on aarch64-darwin with the default stdenv (clang-21
+ libc++-21, self-consistent). The pin predates this repo (initial
import; the 17→18 bump was incidental in a migration commit) and has no
recorded justification.
- Issue option 1 (**keep LLVM 18, use `llvmPackages_18.libcxxStdenv`**)
is **not sufficient**: verified via `nix derivation show` that every
clang-18 wrapper on darwin has `compiler-rt-libc-18.1.8-dev` in
`depsTargetTarget`, and that derivation is built by
`clangWithLibcAndBasicRtAndLibcxx` → `darwin.libcxx` regardless of which
stdenv we hand to chez. Keeping clang-18 would require overriding the
llvm scope's `darwin` argument — deep, fragile surgery against nixpkgs'
design that re-breaks on future libc++ bumps.
- Issue option 3 (re-lock nixpkgs) just rolls the dice on the same
latent mismatch and risks #69's crates.io fix.

## Verification

Cross-evaluated the aarch64-darwin closure from Linux (derivation-level,
pre/post change):

- **Before**: closure of `.#packages.aarch64-darwin.compactc` contains
`llvm-18.1.8`, `clang-18.1.8`, `clang-wrapper-18.1.8`,
`compiler-rt-18.1.8` (built with clang-18 +
`libcxx-21.1.6+apple-sdk-26.5` headers → the reported failure).
- **After**: no LLVM-18 compiler components remain; `chez-scheme-10.4.1`
uses `stdenv-darwin` with `clang-wrapper-21.1.8` (matching
libc++-21.1.6). `.#packages.x86_64-linux.compactc` and
`.#devShells.aarch64-darwin.compiler` still evaluate; alejandra-clean.
- The new `build-macos` job gives the definitive on-runner confirmation.

## CI

Adds `build-macos` to *Compiler Build* (`macos-latest`, arm64): `nix
build .#compactc` + the `tiny.compact` smoke test via `nix develop
.#compiler` — the darwin Nix path had zero macOS coverage, which is why
this rotted silently since #69. Attic push is skipped (Linux-only
cache); the IOG hydra substituter stays configured.

## Notes for reviewers

- `main`/`develop` still pin the pre-#69 nixpkgs, so they currently
build — but they carry the same override and will break on their next
nixpkgs bump. This fix is safe to cherry-pick there as-is.
- Build/CI-only change → please apply the `skip-changelog` label (no
compiler-version bump warranted).

Three small extensions to branch->assert-and-pl-call + the A12/A14
emit clause:

1. **branch->assert-and-pl-call** (rust-passes-walker.ss:2532) now
   admits:
   - `const-decl-only` (skipped — the eventual assignment will emit
     the Rust `let`),
   - `stmt->assignment` (lifted-let initializer; tracked as both a
     pre-stmt for emission AND as a bind for the pl-call's
     expr-resolve),
   - `const-binding` (same).

   Return shape extended from a 5-tuple to a 6-tuple — adds
   `pre-stmts` (ordered list of (var-name . expr) bindings to emit
   as Rust `let`s inside the branch body) between `assert-pair` and
   `src`.

   Assert-only branches (no terminal pl-call) are now also valid
   — the helper returns with `src=#f` when the loop runs out of
   stmts after capturing the assert. (did.compact
   setVerificationMethod's Insert arm is `assert(!verificationMethodExists(...), ...)`
   with no pl-call; the corresponding A12 emit clause now emits an
   empty OpProgramVerify chain for this case.)

2. **A12/A14 emit clause** (rust-passes-streaming.ss):
   - Threaded the new `pre-stmts` field through arm-info and
     else-info.
   - Per arm: emit each pre-stmt as `let <camel-snake name> = <ctor-expr-rust-rendered expr>;`
     inside the branch body BEFORE the assert and OpProgramVerify
     chain. ctor-expr-rust's var-ref fallback uses the same
     `(camel->snake id-sym)` name, so subsequent references inside
     the same branch resolve via Rust lexical scoping (no need to
     extend `local-binds` separately).
   - For arms with `src=#f` (assert-only): `lines` is `'()`, the
     emitted chain is just `OpProgramVerify::new()...build()` —
     a no-op verify that keeps the if-expression's QueryResults
     type uniform across all branches.

3. **did.compact setAlsoKnownAs cross-check**: still byte-stable
   (no regression). The pre-stmts path produces no Rust output
   for setAlsoKnownAs (its branches have no const-decl-only /
   assignment / const-binding shapes), so the emission is unchanged
   for that fixture.

Verified: 24 codegen_regression fixtures byte-stable.

- A14's branch-local binds carrying through to assert-cond-rust:

  id-exported?, matching classify-call's A15 relaxation. Lets a const
  binding to an internal impure helper (e.g. verificationMethodRelationMember)
  emit as `self.<snake>(ctx, ...)?` rather than falling through to the
  generic expression renderer.

Emit (rust-passes-streaming.ss):
- A17 emit clause in the if-tree renders `(assert)(bare-call)` arms as
  `self.<helper>(ctx.clone(), args)?` plus a no-op empty OpProgramVerify
  query, keeping the per-arm QueryResults type uniform across pl-call,
  assert-only, and bare-call arms.
- const-binding's impure-exported case now handles the drifted-ctx
  scenario (ctx-expr is `&_results_N.context` after asserts): splice the
  latest QueryContext into a cloned CircuitContext before the call.

Emit (rust-passes-emit.ss):
- stmt-pure-body-rust refactored into a pure-stmt-rust per-statement
  renderer plus a multi-statement driver. Supports leading
  `assert!(cond, msg);` statements followed by a trailing expression, and
  nested if-then-else (including the 1-arg if form) with multi-statement
  arms. Necessary for assertSupportedVerificationMethod (multi-stmt with
  nested if/else-if/else asserts) and verificationMethodRelationMember
  (5-arm if/else-if returning Boolean). Assertions render via cond-rust
  so ==/or/and/enum-ref are handled correctly.

Net effect: `compactc --rust` now succeeds on did.compact end-to-end
(a 2.7k-line lib.rs). Generated Rust still has downstream type-impl
gaps (EmbeddedGroupAffine FieldRepr/BinaryHashRepr, Fr-array Aligned,
ConstructorContext.current_query_context, schnorr_verify witness) —
these were previously masked by the walker rejecting the body shape
and falling back to `unimplemented!()`. They are the next A/R steps.

Add a purpose-built byte-parity fixture exercising the read-no-arg
ADT gather chain that A20 just fixed. Two exported circuits cover the
same `Set.isEmpty()` / `Map.isEmpty()` shape (the
`(dup) (idx) (size) (push align-0-8) (eq) (popeq)` chain) on two
different container ADTs — confirming A20's expand-vm-code routing
covers both and surfacing any future regression as a hard byte
mismatch on the post-circuit step rather than a silent miscompile.

Source
------

  examples/set_size_fixture.compact
    - One Boolean ledger field per ADT (`flag_set`, `flag_map`) plus
      the matching Set / Map containers, both starting empty.
    - `check_set_empty()` writes `s.isEmpty()` → flag_set.
    - `check_map_empty()` writes `m.isEmpty()` → flag_map.
    - No Set/Map inserts — the read-no-arg gather chain is the only
      A20 surface this fixture is meant to validate, and isolating it
      keeps an independent Set-insert codegen gap from confounding
      the signal.

Generated crate
---------------

  tests-e2e-rust/contracts/set-size-fixture/{Cargo.toml, lib.rs}
    - Emitted by `result/bin/compactc --skip-zk --rust …` from the
      compactc built by `nix build .#compactc` on the A20 branch.
    - Added to the workspace + tests-e2e-rust dev-deps + the
      codegen_regression `FIXTURES` table (so the regen guard picks
      it up automatically alongside the other 24 fixtures).

TS reference capture
--------------------

  tests-e2e-rust/fixtures/capture-set-size-fixture.mjs
    - Three-step capture: afterInit, afterCheckSetEmpty,
      afterCheckMapEmpty. Mirrors the multi-step pattern used by
      `capture-tiny.mjs` (rewrap-envelope + chargedStateFromCtx),
      not the F4–F7 single-step `SmallFixtureTsReference` shape —
      A20's regression signal lives in the *post-circuit* byte
      diff, not the init.

  tests-e2e-rust/fixtures/set-size-fixture-ts-state.json
    - Captured TS reference for the three steps above.

Rust byte-parity test
---------------------

  tests-e2e-rust/tests/set_size_fixture.rs
    - Three tests, one per captured step:
      * set_size_fixture_init_byte_parity
      * set_size_fixture_check_set_empty_byte_parity
      * set_size_fixture_check_map_empty_byte_parity
    - Each builds a fresh Contract, runs the relevant circuit(s),
      wraps the resulting ChargedState in a ContractState envelope
      with the two operations entries (`check_set_empty`,
      `check_map_empty`) the TS driver also registers, and asserts
      `tagged_serialize` of that envelope matches the captured TS
      hex byte-for-byte. A pre-A20 miscompile (gather chain reads
      the Set/Map cell as bool) would surface as a byte mismatch on
      step 2 / step 3.

errors in did.compact's generated lib.rs.

c978df0f76fb1c5cb75aa1e0a20492ba30294d7e.message:
Review feedback from patextreme on #32 (applies identically to #31).

The blanket `compactc --rust` -> `compactc --target rust` substitution in
a55a651 updated the prose but left the surrounding instructions describing
the old interface, so the guide contradicted the compiler it documents.

Five fixes. The reviewer flagged four; the fifth is worse and follows from
the same substitution:

1. The verification step told readers to run
   `compactc --help | grep -- --rust` and showed the old help line. That
   line no longer exists, so a contributor following the Quick Start gets
   no match and may conclude the Rust backend is missing. Now greps
   `--target`, with output verified against the built compiler.

2. Flag notes still presented `--rust` / `--skip-ts` as the primary
   interface, including "Must be combined with `--rust`" — which now
   produces a hard error. Rewritten around `--target`, with the
   list-replaces-default rule stated, and the aliases described as
   transitional with the explicit warning that mixing them with `--target`
   exits 1.

3. "Drop `--rust`" in troubleshooting and the feature matrix -> omit
   `--target rust` / omit `--target`.

4. The `--rust` column header in nine feature-matrix tables, and the
   "Compile your contract with `--rust`" section heading.

5. NOT flagged, and the most serious: the guide's own primary example had
   become `compactc --target rust --skip-zk --skip-ts`, which now EXITS 1
   — the substitution produced a command the compiler rejects. `--skip-ts`
   is subsumed by `--target rust`. Verified the corrected command:
   rc=0, emits Cargo.toml + lib.rs.

Also corrects the parser-behaviour comment in compactc.ss (item 4 of the
review, and the reviewer is right). It claimed "actions can fire while a
clause is merely being attempted". They cannot: the parser threads `act!`
as a thunk chain, each occurrence rebinding it to
`(lambda () (act!) action)` without running it, and invokes the chain only
at the terminal node inside `(let () (act!) . body)` — after the whole
clause has matched. An abandoned attempt calls `(next orig-cl)` and
discards the thunk.

Verified in third_party/compiler/command-line-parsing.ss:606 (the chain)
and :683/:691 (the terminal invocation) rather than taking it on faith.
The shipped logic is unchanged and still correct; only the stated reason
was false, so the comment now gives the real one — validating in the body
keeps the argument checks together and makes diagnostic order
deterministic. Same correction is needed in #30 and the PR bodies, which
repeat the claim.

Also drops a `docs/superpowers/**` link from the guide: that directory is
a dated internal journal and will not exist upstream.

Byte-parity green and unchanged, ./compiler/go exit 0 with zero failures.

d01b2463bfe8f34575eaee0a9f065b8ed5f480d0.message:
R1 walker gap A6 closure. did.compact's `controllerKey(localSecretKey())`
shape (pure-circuit call whose arg is itself a witness call) was
being lowered by the IR into a const-binding RHS, where no witness
hoister fired — the assert clause's witness-subcall hoist machinery
was the only one. Result: compactc threw `witness-inline` because
the witness sub-expression had no rendered name to refer to.

The fix mirrors the assert clause's pattern in the const-binding
clause's `pure-circuit` branch (rust-passes-walker.ss:1792):

  1. collect-witness-subcalls(rhs, witness-id-ht) — walk the full
     RHS for embedded witness calls.
  2. emit-hoisted-witnesses(...) — produces `let _w_<name>_N = ...`
     bind lines plus an alist mapping (function-name + arg expr*) →
     rendered local name.
  3. parameterize current-witness-call-binds around the arg
     rendering so ctor-call-rust's witness branch finds the hoisted
     names instead of throwing witness-inline.
  4. Prepend hoist-lines to pre-lines; thread the updated
     witness-emitted? flag (`we2`) into the loop continuation.

Non-regression: 24 tests-e2e-rust byte-parity fixtures still pass

d52996a0fa109694bf5f00483297bdb3b4e30535.message:
Adopts @patextreme's first interface point from
LFDT-Minokawa/compact#730. Closes #30.

My earlier objection — that `--rust` + `--skip-ts` preserves backward
compatibility — rested on a premise that does not hold: **neither flag
exists upstream**, so there are no invocations to preserve. With `ts`
implied when the flag is absent, today's command lines are untouched
under either design. The real difference is forward compatibility:
`--skip-ts` becomes ambiguous the moment a third backend lands, forcing
exactly the breaking rename `--target` avoids.

| Invocation | TypeScript | Rust |
|---|---|---|
| `compactc c.compact out/` | implied | — |
| `compactc --target rust c.compact out/` | — | ✅ |
| `compactc --target rust --target ts c.compact out/` | ✅ | ✅ |

The list **replaces** the default rather than adding to it. That is what
lets `--target rust` subsume `--rust --skip-ts` with no flag-combination
validation, while keeping "emit both" expressible for the parity
harness. `--skip-zk` stays orthogonal.

## The interesting implementation problem

`third_party/compiler/command-line-parsing.ss` documents:

> If a flag occurs more than once on a command line, the final value of
each corresponding `<var>` is its last specified value.

So a plain `[(--target) (string t)]` clause would have turned `--target
rust --target ts` into **just `ts`**. Silently wrong is worse than
unsupported, so accumulation uses the grammar's per-occurrence `$
<action>` hook instead — no change to vendored code.

Two deliberate choices there:

- **Validation runs in the matched clause body, not in the action.**
Actions can fire while a clause is only being *attempted*, so erroring
inside one could reject a `--target` value on a command line that never
matched that clause.
- **Collection is deduped**, which additionally makes a repeated fire
for a single occurrence harmless.

## Verified against the built binary

The parser docs left the accumulation behaviour genuinely uncertain, so
this was measured, not assumed:

```
(no flag)                    rc=0  ts=YES rust=no
--target ts                  rc=0  ts=YES rust=no
--target rust                rc=0  ts=no  rust=YES
--target rust --target ts    rc=0  ts=YES rust=YES
--target ts --target rust    rc=0  ts=YES rust=YES   (order-independent)
--rust --skip-ts (alias)     rc=0  ts=no  rust=YES
--rust (alias)               rc=0  ts=YES rust=YES

--target go                  rc=1  unknown --target "go"; valid targets are ts, rust
--target rust --target go    rc=1  (rejected even when one value is valid)
--target rust --rust         rc=1  --target cannot be combined with --rust or --skip-ts
--target ts --skip-ts        rc=1  (same)
--skip-ts alone              rc=255 pre-existing "--skip-ts requires --rust" check intact
```

## Transitional aliases

`--rust` / `--skip-ts` keep working as **undocumented** aliases so this
fork's harness and MediaNoxLabs/midnight-identity (which invokes
`compactc --rust --skip-ts`) don't break in the same change. Mixing
`--target` with either is an **error** rather than a silent precedence
rule, so no invocation can be read two ways.

The aliases are fork-transitional and **must not be carried upstream** —
upstream never shipped the flags, so there is nothing there to
deprecate. Added to the #22 hygiene checklist.

## Coverage

The byte-parity gate now invokes `--target rust`, so CI exercises the
new flag. Note the failure mode, which the test comment spells out: a
parsing regression shows up there as *every fixture drifting* (no
`lib.rs` emitted at all), which reads like a codegen catastrophe — check
the flag first.

Byte-parity passing **through `--target rust`** is also direct evidence
the new flag emits byte-identical output to the old one.

## Gates

fmt clean · clippy `-D warnings` clean · **48 test groups** ·
byte-parity green via `--target rust` · **`./compiler/go` exit 0**, zero
failures, both `print-rust` snapshots passing · **`tests-e2e` 50 files,
492 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed**.

Compiler version 0.31.112 → 0.31.113 with a versioned CHANGELOG heading.
Migrated invocations and live docs (AGENT.md, the user guide, rustdoc,
the limitations page); historical records under `docs/superpowers/**`
keep the flags they were written with.

## Merge ordering

**Stacked on #27** (targets `rename/midnight-compact-runtime`, not
`codegen-rust`) because both touch the man-page golden. Retarget to
`codegen-rust` once #27 lands. The ledger-9 counterpart is a separate PR
against `develop`, where the rename already merged via #28.
