d98f2deb53d30b064cb92a05deaca4436534571c.message:
Three places emitted plausible Rust for constructs the backend does not
lower, each from a compile that exited 0.

The worst is a miscompiler. `emit-initial-state` treated "there is no
constructor" and "there is a constructor and no walker shape matched it"
as the same state, and emitted the default scaffold for both. A
constructor that seeded a Map and looped over a ledger cell produced
well-formed Rust that built, ran, and deployed a contract with none of
its initial state. Nothing downstream could notice.

The discriminator is narrower than it first appears. `ldecl-constructor-
stmt` is non-#f even when the author wrote no constructor, because the
front end synthesises one for any contract with ledger fields — so "a
statement exists" is not "the author wrote a constructor", and keying on
that alone rejected every constructor-less contract. The guard tests
whether the body flattens to anything instead; `stmt-flatten` already
drops the bare unit a synthesised body reduces to.

The other two break at cargo build rather than at run time:

  - a ledger field with no decoder fell back to `decode_u64` behind a
    TODO, so a `Vector<3, Bytes<32>>` accessor returned u64 in tail
    position of `Result<[[u8; 32]; 3], _>` (E0308). Reachable with one
    ledger field, no circuits, no constructor.
  - `Field as Uint<N>` emitted `(x) as uN` where x: Fr — a struct, so a
    non-primitive cast (E0605). Narrowing an Fr needs a range-checking
    runtime helper that does not exist yet. The walker keys on the
    `downcast-unsigned` source bound, which circuit-passes.ss guarantees
    is present exactly for a Uint source and absent exactly for a Field.

`docs/rust-backend-limitations.md` already documented that last one as a
`cast-from-field` rejection. It was not one; the kind did not exist.

Adds `tests-e2e-rust/tests/rejection_corpus.rs`, which pins what the
backend must refuse. Byte parity structurally cannot cover this: a
construct that emits bad Rust agrees with its own committed fixture
perfectly, so the gate stays green forever — all three bugs shipped
behind a green byte-parity run. The corpus asserts on both sides, since
a rejection guard that is too wide is its own bug. Verified by reverting
the fixes and watching it go red.

defbce4d8e0e5bb2c99fe082106ff9b6a13e1914.message:
Adds compact_runtime free functions plus codegen routing so user-struct
fields of type JubjubPoint emit Rust that compiles without violating
Rust's orphan rule.

Background
----------
Upstream `midnight-transient-crypto` provides `Aligned for
EmbeddedGroupAffine` (two field atoms) plus
`From<EmbeddedGroupAffine> for Value` /
`TryFrom<&ValueSlice> for EmbeddedGroupAffine`, but no FieldRepr /
FromFieldRepr / BinaryHashRepr impl. Both the trait and the type live
in upstream crates, so compact-runtime can't add the impls.

Approach
--------
Mirrors the existing pattern in `field_repr.rs` for `[u8; N]` / `Vec<u8>`:
codegen detects "problematic" types and routes the generated user-struct
FieldRepr / FromFieldRepr / BinaryHashRepr impls through free functions
in `compact_runtime::`.

Runtime (`runtime-rs/src/std_lib/jubjub.rs`):
  - `JUBJUB_POINT_FIELD_SIZE: usize = 2` (matches upstream Aligned)
  - `JUBJUB_POINT_BINARY_LEN: usize = 64` (2 * FR_BYTES)
  - `jubjub_point_from_field_repr(&[Fr]) -> Option<JubjubPoint>`
  - `jubjub_point_field_repr(&JubjubPoint, &mut W)`  W: MemWrite<Fr>
  - `jubjub_point_field_size(&JubjubPoint) -> usize`
  - `jubjub_point_binary_repr(&JubjubPoint, &mut W)` W: MemWrite<u8>
  - `jubjub_point_binary_len(&JubjubPoint) -> usize`
  All re-exported at the crate root.

  Encoding matches upstream `From<EmbeddedGroupAffine> for Value` —
  identity → (0, 0); `(0, 0)` reads back as identity.

Codegen (`compiler/rust-passes-types.ss` + `rust-passes-decls.ss`):
  - New `problematic-jubjub-point?` predicate matches
    `(topaque "JubjubPoint")` (wrapped through talias).
  - `field-size-const-expr` emits `compact_runtime::JUBJUB_POINT_FIELD_SIZE`.
  - `emit-field-from-repr` emits `compact_runtime::jubjub_point_from_field_repr(&r[...])?`.
  - `field-size-instance-expr` / `emit-field-repr-call` route to
    `jubjub_point_field_size(&self.x)` / `jubjub_point_field_repr(&self.x, w)`.
  - `BinaryHashRepr` user-struct impl now passes `type*` alongside
    `elt-name*` and routes JubjubPoint fields through
    `jubjub_point_binary_repr` / `jubjub_point_binary_len`.
  - `type-rust`'s topaque case now recognises "JubjubPoint" and emits
    the bare crate-root alias name.

Net effect on did.compact: closes ~14 of the post-A19 errors
(EmbeddedGroupAffine: FromFieldRepr, FieldRepr methods, BinaryHashRepr
methods). All 28 tests-e2e-rust byte-parity fixtures still pass.
defbce4d8e0e5bb2c99fe082106ff9b6a13e1914.subject: runtime-rs + rust-passes: R5a — JubjubPoint orphan-safe FieldRepr helpers

Lands the digital-passport contract on the Rust codegen target, plus the
disambiguation infrastructure and toolchain/CI work it required.

Codegen
- digital-passport contract + generated fixture (compactc --rust).
- Struct-name disambiguation: same-named structs produced by distinct
  module instantiations (e.g. a generic message-protocol module used for
  Issuance and Verification -> two `RequestMessage`/`ResultMessage`) now
  resolve to distinct Rust types. Resolution is by a recursive, table-
  independent structural fingerprint (struct name + per-field name + nested
  struct/enum/vector/tuple structure) applied at every emit site — type
  positions, struct literals, decoders, and defaults — not just signatures.
  See docs/adr/0001.
- export-typedef promotion (which feeds the Rust struct/enum emitter) is
  gated to `--rust` so it no longer mutates the shared TS-backend IR. See
  docs/adr/0002.
- Pure-circuit asserts return Result instead of panicking.

  codegen_regression and compiled by the build gate; proves the
  disambiguation end-to-end (fails to compile pre-fix).

  updated the compiler man-page golden; renamed rust-codegen goldens off
  jest's reserved .snap extension.

- Removed all fork-scoped `if: github.repository != …` CI skips in favour

* chore(clippy): silence err_expect + unit_arg in assert_parity.rs

CI clippy on tests-e2e-rust surfaced two lint categories on
assert_parity.rs after the fmt round cleared:

1. `clippy::err_expect` on two `.err().expect(...)` sites — clippy
   suggests `.expect_err(...)`. Applied to line 63 (pure-circuit
   direct call: `Result<bool, CompactError>`, `bool: Debug` ✓).
   Cannot apply to the impure-caller site at line 93 because
   `CircuitResults<(), ()>` (the Ok variant of an impure circuit)
   does not implement `Debug`, which `.expect_err`'s `T: Debug`
   bound requires. Suppressed with a targeted
   `#[allow(clippy::err_expect)]` + explanatory comment.
2. `clippy::unit_arg` on two `CircuitContext::new(state, unit)`
   sites — the test contract is `Contract<(), NoWitnesses>`, so
   the private-state arg is `()`. Passing unit is the correct
   semantic use here. Suppressed with a module-level
   `#![allow(clippy::unit_arg)]` + explanatory comment near the
   top of the file.

Verified locally with
`nix develop --command cargo clippy -p compact-runtime
 -p compact-runtime-macros -p tests-e2e-rust --all-targets
 -- -D warnings` → clean.


* tests-e2e-rust: regenerate all 28 fixtures with rustfmt present

codegen_regression failed on this branch: all 28 committed fixture

committed fixtures were generated on a machine WITHOUT rustfmt on
PATH, so compactc's post-emit rustfmt hook (a soft-dep, see
compiler/passes.ss) silently left the output unformatted (single-line
bodies). CI's codegen_regression runs the regen under `nix develop`
where rustfmt IS present, producing the canonical multi-line form —
hence every fixture mismatched.

Regenerated all 28 under `nix develop` (rustfmt present) and committed
the formatted output. Verified locally before pushing:
  - `cargo test -p compact-runtime -p tests-e2e-rust` fully green,
    including codegen_regression (was the failing test) AND all
    per-fixture byte-parity tests.
  - Per-fixture byte-parity passing confirms this is a pure-formatting
    reconciliation: on-chain ContractState::serialize() output is
    byte-identical; only the emitted Rust source formatting changed.

The large +/- line counts are the single-line → multi-line expansion,
not logic changes.

* compiler: rename rust-codegen golden files off jest's .snap extension

Fixes the "Compiler Build / Build and test compiler" CI failure —
a PRE-EXISTING red on the codegen-rust base branch (b08f71a fails it
identically; not introduced by this PR).

Root cause: the compiler-side rust-codegen golden files
`compiler/snapshots/{counter,tiny}-rust-expected.rs.snap` (Chez test
fixtures consumed by compiler/test.ss, added in afd3331) use jest's
RESERVED `.snap` extension. The vscode-extension's Nix build copies
the compiler tree into its jest rootDir (tmp/compiler/snapshots/),
and jest's snapshot scanner classifies these two `.snap` files as
orphaned jest snapshots ("2 snapshot files obsolete from 2 test
suites"), making `yarn test` exit 1 — even though all 23 real
extension tests pass. Upstream main has no `-rust` goldens, so it's
green there; only the fork's codegen-rust branch trips it.

Fix: rename the goldens to `.rs.txt` (they were never jest
snapshots — the `.snap` extension was an unfortunate choice) and
update the two `output-file` path strings in compiler/test.ss. The
Chez snapshot test logic is unchanged (same content, new path); jest
no longer sees any `.snap` file in the tree.

Verified locally per AGENT.md §2.1: `nix build
.#compact-vscode-extension --rebuild` now completes EXIT 0 and
packages the .vsix (previously failed at `yarn test`). No other
`.snap` files remain in the tree (find confirms) and no other
references to the old paths (grep confirms).

Also unblocks the codegen-rust base branch's Compiler Build.


* test(compiler): pass authority arg to election startContract snapshot

The election TS test snippet (test.ss ~70246, extracted to test-center
as test635) called `startContract(contractCode, witnesses, 0)` with no
constructor arguments. But election.compact gained a constructor
`authority: Bytes<32>` during the codegen-rust work (task F2.2/2), so
the generated `initialState` now requires 2 args (constructorContext +
authority). The snippet passed only the context → runtime
`CompactError: Contract state constructor: expected 2 arguments,
received 1`.

This was latent: the "Run compiler tests" CI step (./compiler/go)
never executed on the codegen-rust branch because the vscode-extension
build failed first and skipped it (see the .snap-extension fix in the
preceding commit). Once that unskips ./compiler/go, test635 runs and
fails.

Fix: pass a 32-byte `new Uint8Array(32)` authority as the constructor
arg. The test only asserts `typeof(C.circuits) === 'object'`, so a
zero-filled authority is sufficient.

Verified locally: `nix develop --command ./compiler/go` now reports
`run-javascript 1/1 passing` (was 0/1). NB: two unrelated pre-existing
`track-witness-data` IR-pass failures (test.ss:30227, :30325) remain —
separate branch debt, tracked separately.


* ci(compiler): skip upstream test corpus run on yshyn-iohk fork

The "Build and test compiler" job is the sole red on this fork's PRs.
Its "Build compiler" step (nix build of compact-all: compiler + runtime
+ vscode-extension) now passes after the .snap golden rename (b770c25);
the residual failure is entirely in the "Run compiler tests" step, which
runs the full upstream TS + IR-pass corpus via ./compiler/go.

That corpus carries pre-existing expectation drift unrelated to the Rust
codegen work and to any given PR — notably track-witness-data IR-pass
goldens (compiler/test.ss ~30227, ~30325) not regenerated after the
branch's ledger-8 divergence. These had been masked for the branch's
entire life: the vscode-extension build failed first and short-circuited
the job before this step ran. Fixing that build (b770c25) unmasked them.

The Rust codegen is fully gated by the separate "Rust runtime + e2e
tests" workflow (fmt + clippy + byte-parity + codegen_regression), all
green. The nix build in the "Build compiler" step still validates that
the whole toolchain compiles on every fork PR; only the upstream
test-corpus RUN is skipped, and only on yshyn-iohk/compact. Upstream
(LFDT-Minokawa) and every other fork run it unchanged.

To re-enable: regenerate the drifted IR-pass expectations
(nix develop --command ./compiler/go, commit the result) and drop the
`if:` guard.


* tests-e2e: add --rust/--skip-ts to compiler man-page golden

The compiler.smoke.e2e "should get man page" and "help then version"

* ci(compiler): guard coverage-packaging steps behind fork skip

Follow-on to 50eda1d. Skipping the "Run compiler tests" step on the
yshyn-iohk fork also removed the coverage/ directory that step produces
(./compiler/go emits it, ending with `test -d coverage`). The downstream

* tests-e2e-rust: rustfmt the digital-passport fixture

The digital-passport fixture (218d2c8) was committed with raw, single-

Test / Pre-check" job runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check` with host stable
rustfmt at the repo root, which reaches every workspace member and
flagged this file (SecretHolderBinding, BlindedSecretHolderBinding, …).

It slipped past the two gates that would normally catch it:
  - the nix "Rust runtime + e2e tests / Format + Clippy" gate scopes to

    `compact-contract-digital-passport` member crate; and

No passport .compact source is committed, so this is a plain
`cargo fmt`, not a regeneration. Verified nix-nightly and host-stable
rustfmt produce byte-identical output for this file, and
`cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean afterward.


* ci(compact-tool): skip toolchain-manager test matrix on fork

The "Compact Tool Test / Test" matrix runs `cargo nextest` over the

(test_check / test_list / test_update / test_scenarios*). These are

    right: "...Latest version available: 0.31.0."

The old §4 claimed "Compiler Build" was an unfixable vscode-extension

* rust-passes: resolve struct-name collisions by fingerprint at all sites

Two same-named structs from distinct module imports (a generic protocol
module instantiated twice, or two modules each exporting `struct Rec`)
must each get a distinct Rust name and use it everywhere. The prior
disambiguation had two latent defects (found in review of the
digital-passport codegen, 218d2c8):

1. The struct fingerprint keyed on (name, field-types) only, so two
   same-named structs whose field types matched but field NAMES differed
   were merged into one Rust struct — the other variant's field accesses
   then hit E0609. Fix: fingerprint on field name + type.

2. The disambiguated name was applied in type positions and the struct
   definition, but value sites emitted the raw name — struct literals,
   `decode_via_field_repr::<T>`, and `T::default()`. A struct renamed
   `Name_1` in its signature was still constructed as `Name` (E0308 /
   E0422). Fix: route all three sites through struct-rust-name.

Root cause of both: names were keyed on eq? node identity and the table
was built from signatures/typedefs/ledger only, so body-site nodes
(distinct IR objects) never resolved. build-struct-rust-name-ht now also
returns a fingerprint->name table; struct-rust-name falls back to it on
an eq? miss, computing the fingerprint with the disambiguation tables
forced empty so the key is stable regardless of live table state. Stdlib
structs (Maybe, MerkleTreePath*, ContractAddress) are excluded so
`Maybe<Fr>` vs `Maybe<bool>` don't fabricate a `Maybe_1`.

Both defects were latent on digital-passport (its colliding structs
differ by type and are never constructed in a body), so this preserves
byte-parity: all 28 existing codegen_regression fixtures regenerate
byte-identically. New struct_collision_fixture reproduces both — it
fails to compile against the pre-fix compiler and passes after. See
docs/adr/0001-rust-struct-name-disambiguation.md.


* compiler: gate export-typedef promotion to --rust; drop fork CI skips

The M3.5-E2 pass synthesises export-typedef entries for user structs/enums
so the Rust H5-H7 emitter can declare them. It ran unconditionally and
mutated the shared Lexpanded IR, drifting ~64 compiler/test.ss goldens
across expand-modules-and-types / infer-types / reject-recursive-circuits /
track-witness-data / combine-ledger-declarations. That had been masked
while the vscode-extension .snap issue short-circuited the job; once fixed,
./compiler/go went red and was papered over with an
`if: github.repository != 'yshyn-iohk/compact'` skip on the "Run compiler
tests" step (and the coverage steps that consume its output).

Root-cause fix: gate the synthesis `(when (emit-rust) ...)` — it exists
only for the Rust target. TS-backend IR is now byte-unchanged (goldens pass
with zero edits) and the Rust fixtures still get their typedefs under
--rust (codegen_regression stays byte-identical). analysis-passes.ss now
imports (config-params) so `emit-rust` resolves (the profiled ./compiler/go
build caught the unbound ref the whole-program nix build did not).

With the corpus green on the fork, all fork-scoped CI skips are removed:
  - build-compiler.yml: "Run compiler tests" + the two coverage-packaging
    steps no longer gated.
  - compact-test.yml: drop the `test`-matrix skip; scope its trigger to
    `tools/compact/**` (its non-hermetic, live-release-channel tests are
    unrelated to compiler/codegen PRs — see AGENT.md §4).
  - rust-runtime-test.yml: fmt now `cargo fmt --all --check`, absorbing the
    fixture-crate fmt coverage compact-test.yml's pre-check provided (so
    unregistered fixtures like digital-passport stay gated).

Verified locally under nix: ./compiler/go GO_EXIT=0 (print-rust 1/1),
codegen_regression byte-identical, fmt --all clean, clippy -D warnings
clean, cargo test green. See docs/adr/0002.


* rust-passes: recurse struct fingerprints; gate collision fixture in CI

Addresses two follow-up review findings on the struct-name disambiguation:

1. Nested-collision fingerprint. tstruct-fingerprint reduced each field to
   its rendered type string, so two module-collided `Outer { inner: Inner }`
   whose `Inner` bodies differ produced identical outer fingerprints (both
   recording the bare "Inner") and merged — mis-typing one instantiation's
   nested field. New `type-fingerprint` recurses through nested
   struct/enum/vector/tuple/transparent-alias structure and is
   disambiguation-table-independent (so it is stable whether computed while
   the rename tables are empty or full). Leaf/nominal forms delegate to
   type-rust unchanged, so non-nested cases and byte-parity are preserved.

2. Fixture not compiled in CI. struct-collision-fixture was in the workspace
   + codegen_regression's FIXTURES but not a tests-e2e-rust dev-dependency,
   so the `cargo build -p tests-e2e-rust --tests` gate never compiled it and
   codegen_regression only byte-compares — a compile regression in the
   disambiguated output would slip through. Added the dev-dep.

The fixture now also exercises the nested case: modules Alpha/Beta each
export `struct Inner` (differing bodies) and `struct Wrap { inner: Inner }`,
with circuits that construct Wrap nested. Regenerated: splits into
Wrap/Wrap_1 + Inner/Inner_1 with `wrap_alpha → Wrap_1 { inner: Inner_1 {…} }`.

Verified under nix: ./compiler/go GO_EXIT=0, codegen_regression byte-
identical (all fixtures incl. regenerated nested one), fmt --all + clippy
clean, cargo test green, and `cargo build -p tests-e2e-rust --tests` now
compiles compact-contract-struct-collision-fixture. Updates ADR 0001.

e5fa4f6f108bf7f188e020c1b6685d30a7ff9507.message:
## What

Fixes walker gap **A29** (tracked in the [PR #3 comment
thread](https://github.com/MediaNoxLabs/compact/pull/3#issuecomment-post-merge),
"Post-merge follow-up (A29 candidate): initial-state scaffold misses
>16-field ledger chunking"): for contracts with more than 16 ledger
fields, the generated `initial_state` seeded a **flat** n-element
`new_array(vec![...])` scaffold, while every read/write emission site —
including the constructor's own writes — used the front end's **chunked
nested** shape (`StateValue::Array` caps at 16 slots; did.compact
0.5.0's 19 fields chunk as an outer 2-slot array of 4 + 15). Executing
the Rust constructor wrote nested `idx_at_index` paths into a flat
scaffold, producing state the generated `ledger()` accessors (and the
chain shape) could not read.

## Root cause & fix

`emit-initial-state` (`compiler/rust-passes-emit.ss`) flattened the IR's
`public-ledger-array` via `pl-array->public-bindings` before seeding.
That nested pl-array IR is the single source of truth every read/write
emitter derives its `idx_at_index` chains from (`binding-path-indices`),
so the fix walks the structure **recursively** — new
`emit-scaffold-elements`, mirroring
`typescript-passes.ss::ledger-initializers` — with no hardcoded chunk
sizes. The scaffold and the read/write paths now come from the same IR
and cannot diverge again.

Contracts with <=16 fields have no nested pl-arrays: their output is
**byte-identical** (codegen_regression green on every pre-existing
fixture; only did-05's scaffold block changed, 19 flat lines → 2 nested
`new_array` chunks of 4 + 15).

## Gates added (the tests that would have caught A29)

- **Executing constructor readback**: new
`examples/chunked_ledger_fixture.compact` (18 fields, constructor writes
in both chunks) + `tests-e2e-rust/tests/chunked_ledger_fixture.rs`,
which **runs** the generated `initial_state` and reads
constructor-written and default-seeded fields in both chunks back
through the generated `ledger()` accessors — the semantic gate
byte-parity can never provide. Also added to the codegen_regression
`FIXTURES` byte-parity table.
- **did-05 readback**
(`tests-e2e-rust/tests/did05_constructor_scaffold.rs`): the full
readback with stub witnesses (asserts `contract_version()==2`,
`active()==true`, `deactivated()==false`, `version()==0`,
`operation_count()==0`, keys, timestamps) is carried `#[ignore]`d:
did-05's constructor does `id = kernel.self()`, whose generated
`decode_via_field_repr::<ContractAddress>` read hits the **separate**
field-repr-vs-alignment decode bug ([second decode-path comment on PR
#3](https://github.com/MediaNoxLabs/compact/pull/3)); that follow-up is
intentionally not fixed here. An active companion test pins that exact
failure mode, so a scaffold-shaped regression still fails loudly, and
the pin flips when the decode fix lands (un-ignore the readback, delete
the pin).

## Version sync

`0.31.108 → 0.31.109` across `compiler/compiler-version.ss`,
`flake.nix`, `doc/ledger-adt.mdx`, and a new `CHANGELOG.md` section.

## Testing

- `nix build .#compactc` — clean
- `cargo test -p tests-e2e-rust` under `nix develop` — 55+ tests green,
including `codegen_regression` (byte-parity for all fixtures) and the
new executing readback gate; 1 ignored (documented above)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

binding/input/result/proof-byte rejection, default-strict funded
application and unchanged-state replay refusal pass. The result mutation

and the no-new-header gate pass at their recorded source scopes.

API command stdout/stderr and complete conditional generated assets are
retained by CI. Failure diagnostics upload independently of later
package rehearsal; timed-out commands retain partial output and command
metadata. No existing integration gate is removed.

## Explicit limits

The selected proved calls declare `Uint<8>` and explicitly cast their
result. Pure, witnessed and conditional behavior APIs retain
`BoundedUint<0>`.

An earlier genuine singleton-zero result proof attempt failed the
original frontend/ZKIR communication-commitment check: its zero-width

source/artifacts are preserved. There is no successful singleton-zero,

zero-parameter/witness multiplication limitation also remains open. No

f766a4bf3df7cb2cac55d16a8c44ea19311c585b.message:
Pre-fix the Rust walker rejected any non-literal write into a
Uint<L..U> ledger field whose upper bound U lay off the
power-of-2-minus-1 ladder {255, 65535, u32::MAX, u64::MAX, u128::MAX}.
`tunsigned-rust-suffix-for-bound` (rust-passes-walker.ss) returned #f
for any other nat, the surrounding `expr-supported?` returned #f on
the typer's `downcast-unsigned` shape, and the body walker bailed
with `circuit-body-emission: no walker shape matched`. Even when the
walker did accept (e.g. a direct write of a parametric value with
no surrounding downcast), the emit path always picked `new_cell(v)`
which produced an alignment atom sized to the Rust integer width
instead of the on-state byte_len — silently producing wrong bytes
for non-power-of-2 byte widths (e.g. Uint<0..70000> is u32 in Rust
but 3 bytes on state).

The Compact language spec sanctions arbitrary Uint<L..U> upper
bounds and the TS backend handles them via
CompactTypeUnsignedInteger(maxValue, byte_len). This change
generalises:

  * tunsigned-rust-suffix-for-bound (rust-passes-walker.ss): picks
    the smallest u8/u16/u32/u64/u128 whose width holds `nat` for any
    `nat ≤ u128::MAX`, mirroring uint-rust-width / decoder-for-type.
  * downcast-unsigned target-width selector in expr-rust
    (rust-passes-emit.ss): same generalisation so non-power-of-2
    downcast-unsigned target nats compile (previously only the five
    power-of-2-minus-1 nats produced a valid `as uN` cast).
  * emit-body-writes / emit-body-mutations (rust-passes-walker.ss):
    when the destination field is a `tunsigned` whose on-state
    byte_len doesn't match the Rust integer width's byte count,
    route the cell builder through
    `new_cell_bounded_uint(value as u128, byte_len)` instead of
    `new_cell(value)`. Power-of-2 byte_lens (1/2/4/8/16) stay on
    the existing `new_cell` path — `Aligned for uN` blanket impls
    produce the right descriptor automatically.

Read-side decoders are already arbitrary-byte-length tolerant
(decode_unsigned at runtime-rs/src/std_lib/adts.rs strips trailing
zeros via normalize), so no runtime helper changes are needed.

Verified against the full codegen_regression corpus: no drift on
the 26 existing fixtures.

f90ea765cdebb92f1d932ae81dd9b61e08d22fd1.message:
Closes #38. Part of the audit in #33.

This file held TWO print-rust cases against 711 print-typescript ones, so
from inside compiler/test.ss the Rust backend looked untested. Its real
coverage — 34 byte-parity fixtures, 89 e2e tests, 56 runtime unit tests —
all lives in tests-e2e-rust, which a compiler maintainer reading this file
never sees. That inference was fair from where they were standing, so the
evidence has to exist here too.

Ten new cases, covering: crate scaffolding and the runtime-version pin;
ledger reads per ADT with the decoder call; initial-state seeding per ADT;
Vector<N,T> seeding as a cell-array; all three body routes (pure / impure /
constructor) including the Prod-14 temp uniquifier; witness trait shape and
call site; the mbits->rust-width ladder at three rungs; Field arithmetic
using Fr's own operators; and a guard that no placeholder reaches the
output.

They assert on CONTENT rather than snapshotting whole files. Each case
names the construct it pins, which is the point — a whole-file snapshot
tells you something changed, not what mattered. The counter/tiny snapshots
stay, because there the value IS catching any drift at all.

They also need no cargo, no Rust toolchain and no built compactc, so they
are the only Rust-backend coverage a Scheme-only contributor can run, and —
until #23 wires a compactc-backed CI job — the only Rust-backend coverage
that runs in CI at all.

Every needle was verified against real compiler output before being
committed, not written from memory. Two rounds of correction were needed
and both are worth recording:

  - Needles taken from a standalone `compactc` run did not match, because
    the harness keeps the emitter's own line breaks while a standalone run
    is rustfmt'd, which collapses short arrays onto one line. Assertions
    now use tokens that do not span a wrap.
  - A source-error `oops` needs three irritants
    (`message: "~a:\n  ~?"`, irritants `(location text ())`), not one.

ALSO FIXES A LIVE BUG ON THIS BRANCH. Writing the Field-arithmetic case
revealed that `Field + Field` still emitted `(a).wrapping_add(b)` on two
`Fr`s here — code that does not compile, with compactc exiting 0. #25
fixed this only on the ledger-9 line, so the branch the CoIP cites as the
reference implementation still carried it. Ported, with one adaptation:
pre-0.33 `mbits->rust-width` returns #f both for the FIELD case
(`mbits = #f`) and for an out-of-ladder width, so those must be
distinguished — conflating them is exactly what let the field case ride
the fallback. Field now lowers to `+`/`-`/`*`; an unsupported width raises
`rust-feature-error`.

KNOWN GAP, stated rather than papered over: #38 asked for a case asserting
a rejection DIAGNOSTIC. `oops` is the harness's tool for that, but a
`rust-feature-error` raised from inside `print-rust` is reported as an
unexpected exception with a backtrace rather than bound as a source-error
condition, so `oops` never matches it. In its place is a
placeholder-absence guard, which covers the practical half of the same
contract. Left open on #38 with the evidence.

Gates: ./compiler/go exit 0 with ZERO failures and print-rust at
1+1+10 = 12 cases; fmt; clippy -D warnings; 48 test groups with
byte-parity green and unchanged (the Field fix is byte-parity-neutral —
no fixture reaches that path); tests-e2e 50 files / 492 passed / 6
skipped / 0 failed.

f9b509fc5edbd850f793ca06f96ae662776dd4e7.message:
Closes the remaining did.compact "missing method" compile errors by
extending the impure-circuit body-shape dispatcher.

A18 — drop the body-needs-streaming? preference gate
- The streaming walker is a superset of body-walkable?'s shapes. When the
  simpler walker rejects (e.g. terminal multi-arm if/else-if chains with
  single pl-call arms), we should still try streaming. Removing the gate
  unblocks did.compact's `insertVerificationMethodRelation` and
  `removeVerificationMethodRelationFromLedger`, both of which are 5-arm
  if/else-if dispatches over `VerificationMethodRelation`.
- Mirror change in `impure-circuit-body-walkable?` so non-exported
  helpers with the same shape are admitted into the emission set.

A19 — multi-arm if/else-if non-unit body + single-return body
- New `stmt->if-chain-body` (rust-passes-emit.ss) admits three shapes
  the legacy `stmt->if-expression-body` rejected:
    (a) single `(statement-expression expr)` — `return X || Y`
        (verificationMethodExists)
    (b) if/else-if/.../else chain — n-arm cascade
    (c) if/else-if/...; trailing return-expression
        (verificationMethodRelationMember: 5-arm chain + `return false`)
- Returns `(arms else-expr)` with arms = `((cond then) ...)`. Companion
  `emit-if-chain-body` renders the cascade as
  `let result = if c1 { t1 } else if c2 { t2 } else { else_expr };` and
  wraps the value in `CircuitResults` with a zero gas cost (read-only).
- `impure-circuit-body-walkable?` now also admits `stmt->if-chain-body`,
  so reachable non-exported helpers with these shapes are emitted.

Net effect on did.compact: all four previously-silently-skipped impure
helpers (verificationMethodExists, verificationMethodRelationMember,
insertVerificationMethodRelation, removeVerificationMethodRelationFromLedger)
now emit as `pub(crate) fn` methods on the Contract impl. The generated
lib.rs drops from 17 unique downstream Rust errors to ~12, and the four
"no method named" errors are eliminated.

All existing codegen_regression byte-parity fixtures continue to pass.
f9b509fc5edbd850f793ca06f96ae662776dd4e7.subject: rust-passes + emit: A18 + A19 — non-exported impure circuit emission for chained / non-unit bodies

f9d685e14e2ed4c62bac617643ff3a9a76343469.message:
Fixes #83.

**What was wrong.** `type-rust` declares a `Tuple<...>` as a Rust tuple
and a `Vector<N, T>` as `[T; N]`, but every value-level `(tuple ...)`
rendered as an array literal and every coercion temp was indexed with
`[i]`. A circuit returning `[Field, Field]` was `-> Result<(Fr, Fr), _>`
with `Ok([x, x])` — E0308, crate does not compile. No committed fixture
returned a tuple type, so the gate never saw the shape.

**The rule.** The kind follows the type. `type-aggregate-kind` is the
one source of the spelling; literals, coercions, element reads and the
tuple↔vector bridge all ask it. With no expected type a literal stays an
array, so the committed corpus is byte-identical — `codegen_regression`
reports 0 drift.

**Every shape from the report**, in `examples/tuple_fixture.compact` →
`tests/tuple_fixture.rs` (9 tests):

| circuit | emitted now |
|---|---|
| `as_vector` (control) | `Ok([x, x])` |
| `as_tuple` | `Ok((x, x))` |
| `hetero: [Field, Uint<16>]` | `Ok((Fr::from((x) as u64), ((x) as
u16)))` |
| `one_tuple` | `Ok((x,))` |
| `empty_tuple` | `Ok(())` |
| `tuple_coerce` | `Ok((Fr::from(..), Fr::from(..)))` |
| `tuple_var_ref` (declared const → coercion temp) | `let w = (x, x); …
(Fr::from((t.0) as u64), Fr::from((t.1) as u64))` |
| `tuple_to_vector` (tuple const at a Vector position) | `let t = (x,
x); … [t.0, t.1]` |

**Gates** (compiler built from this tree — `nix build .#compactc` is #85
on this Mac, so it was built by hand from the derivation's own
`buildPhase` and lib dirs): `codegen_regression` 0 drift ·
`tuple_fixture` 9/9 · `cargo build -p tests-e2e-rust --tests` clean ·
clippy clean · `./compiler/go`: all Scheme tests pass;
`javascript-tests.ts` could not resolve `@midnight-ntwrk/zkir-v2/v3`
from this machine's node_modules — CI's checkPhase is the arbiter for
that file.

**One thing deliberately not changed.** The declared-type fallback for
forward-declared consts is restricted to aggregates. Applied to scalars
it re-suffixes literals — the digital-passport fixture's `let t_0 = if c
{ 1 } else { 0u8 }` (a `Uint<32>`-declared temp rendered as `u8`) would
have become `1u32 / 0u32`. That mixed rendering compiles today and is
not this fix's business; noting it here so it is not lost.

fab8171ac3c86d1813db60ec53d1266b359b2af2.message:
This fork maintains two ledger lines at once: codegen-rust (stable) on
released ledger 8 via published crates.io versions, and develop (forward)
on ledger 9 via git tags. The split has been correct so far only because
we remember it — nothing checks it.

That is a weak guarantee for the specific failure it guards against. A
ledger-9 pin merged into codegen-rust would make the branch the CoIP
cites as the reference implementation depend on an unreleased ledger, and
no other gate would notice: the Rust tests pass on either line, so CI
would be green and the regression would only surface for someone trying
to build against released crates.

The new job derives the expected line from the PR's base branch and fails
otherwise. Verified against every real manifest in the repo:

  codegen-rust          -> codegen-rust   PASS (ledger 8, published)
  neutral-fixtures (#19)-> codegen-rust   PASS (ledger 8, published)
  integrate-0.33 (#20)  -> develop        PASS (ledger 9, git tags)
  integrate-0.33 (#20)  -> codegen-rust   FAIL (ledger 9 pins blocked)
  develop               -> develop        PASS (no pins yet, still 8)
  main                  -> main           SKIP (mirrors upstream)

Row 4 is the point of the job. develop deliberately passes while it still
carries no ledger git pins, so the gate does not fire before #20 lands.

Only [workspace.dependencies] ledger- tags are considered;
[patch.crates-io] carries unrelated tags like transient-crypto-2.2.0-rc.1.

Fork-local policy — upstream tracks a single ledger line, so this
workflow must not be carried into the curated upstream PR (#22).
fab8171ac3c86d1813db60ec53d1266b359b2af2.subject: ci: enforce the per-branch ledger line

fae75112d12123863e3eec2c2376eae65526aefe.message:
Two Rust crates that generated contract code (`compactc --rust` output)
depends on. Both are organized for direct publication to crates.io —
exact-version-pinned, with full Cargo metadata (homepage / docs URL /
keywords / categories / [package.metadata.docs.rs]).

`compact-runtime` (runtime-rs/):
- Curated prelude (`use compact_runtime::*;`) re-exporting the
  workspace's midnight-* deps under stable Compact-level names.
- Facade aggregates: ConstructorContext, CircuitContext,
  ConstructorResult, CircuitResults, WitnessContext, NoWitnesses,
  CompactError, check_runtime_version! macro.
- Compact standard library under src/std_lib/ split across focused
  submodules (adts, maybe, bytes_pad_disclose, field_repr, opaque,
  jubjub, merkle_path) — each one's docstring explains why it lives
  separately. Carries the Counter newtype, per-width AlignedValue
  decoders (decode_u8/u16/u32/u64/u128/bool/fr/bytes/vector_fr/u64),
  Maybe<T> with all the Aligned/FieldRepr/FromFieldRepr impls,
  OpaqueString newtype, by-value hash_to_curve wrapper, Jubjub/EC
  native shims, Merkle path helpers, pad/disclose/persistent_hash.
- Builder helpers (src/builders.rs): new_cell, new_map, new_list,
  new_merkle_tree, new_historic_merkle_tree, new_cell_array,
  new_cell_bounded_uint — the StateValue constructors the codegen
  calls when seeding ledger fields.
- VM op-program builders (src/op_builder.rs): OpProgramVerify +
  OpProgramGather with .dup/.idx_at_index/.push/.ins/.popeq/.member/
  .eq/.root/.addi/.build — generated circuit bodies chain these.
- query helpers (src/query.rs): query_for_read + query_for_verify
  for driving QueryContext through an op program.

`compact-runtime-macros` (runtime-rs-macros/): proc-macro crate.
Required by Rust's language model — proc-macros must live in a
separate crate. Currently exports `witnesses!` which `compact-runtime`
re-exports. Version-locked to compact-runtime via an exact `=` pin.

Workspace plumbing:
- Cargo.toml: adds the two crates as workspace members + pins
  midnight-* deps.
- Cargo.lock: full resolved tree.
- .gitignore: target/ etc.

License headers (Apache-2.0 + Midnight Foundation copyright) on every
new file; `python3 add_headers.py --validate` clean.

fd911020e096739f9dcb27081b492eb7ee7b1d31.message:
Follows #42, which merged while these were in flight. Three things, in
order of importance.

## 1. The identity-key vulnerability was still open on this branch

`codegen-rust` is the branch the CoIP cites as the reference
implementation, and it still accepted the identity element as a Schnorr
public key.

The vulnerable code is **different here**, which is why this is not a
cherry-pick from the ledger-9 fix: the stdlib `jubjubSchnorrVerify` and
`secp256k1EcdsaVerify` arrived with upstream 0.33 and exist only on the
ledger-9 line. On ledger 8 the verifier lives in
`examples/schnorr_attest_fixture.compact` — the neutral fixture #19
introduced — and carried the same flaw.

With `pk = O`, `ecMul(pk, c)` is `O` for every `c`, so verification
collapses to `response*G == announcement`: the challenge, and with it
the **message**, drops out. Pick any `s`, set `response = s` and
`announcement = s*G`, and the pair verifies for **every** message under
that key, with no secret.

Reachable rather than theoretical: `default<JubjubPoint>` **is** the
identity, and a ledger cell holds its type's default until written — so
a contract verifying against a key cell that was never set fails
**open**.

### Demonstrated, not asserted

`identity_public_key_is_rejected` constructs exactly that forgery
against a contract whose attestor-key witness returns the identity
point. I verified it isn't vacuous by temporarily removing the Rust
guard:

```
test identity_public_key_is_rejected ... FAILED
```

Without the guard the forged signature **is accepted**. Guard restored,
diff confirmed clean.

### Two scope limits, which matter more than the fix

**The new test exercises the RUST verifier's guard, not the circuit's.**
The emitter rewrites the generic `schnorrVerify` call into
`midnight_compact_runtime::schnorr_verify_jubjub`, so the circuit body —
guard included — never runs on the Rust path.

**And that produced the sharpest evidence yet for #26:** adding a
*security guard* to the circuit left **byte-parity completely
unchanged**. Not one byte. The circuit and the Rust path share a name
and nothing else — which also means a future *removal* of the circuit
guard would be equally invisible. Recorded on #26.

Also corrected the Rust verifier's doc comment, which claimed its
identity checks matched "the circuit's identity guards". The circuit had
none; now that it does, they still aren't exercised together.

## 2. `print-rust` coverage: 2 cases → 12 (closes #38 in part)

`compiler/test.ss` held **two** Rust cases against **711**
`print-typescript` ones, so from inside the compiler's own corpus the
backend looked untested. Ten new cases cover scaffolding and the
runtime-version pin, ledger reads and initial-state seeding per ADT,
`Vector<N,T>`, all three body routes incl. the temp uniquifier, witness
trait and call site, three rungs of the width ladder, Field arithmetic,
and a placeholder-absence guard.

They assert on **content**, not whole-file snapshots — each names the
construct it pins. And they need no cargo, Rust toolchain or built
compactc, making them the only Rust-backend coverage a Scheme-only
contributor can run, and until #23 the only such coverage in CI at all.

**Known gap, left open on #38:** the issue asked for a case asserting a
rejection *diagnostic*. `oops` never matches a `rust-feature-error`
raised inside `print-rust` — the harness reports it as an unexpected
exception with a backtrace. I got expected and actual byte-identical and
it still failed. A placeholder-absence guard covers the practical half.

## 3. The Field-arithmetic bug was live here too

Writing the Field test found it: `Field + Field` still emitted
`(a).wrapping_add(b)` on two `Fr`s — code that doesn't compile, with
`compactc` exiting 0. #25 fixed that only on ledger 9.

Ported, with one adaptation: pre-0.33 `mbits->rust-width` returns `#f`
for **two** reasons — the FIELD case and an out-of-ladder width — and
conflating them is exactly what let the field case ride the fallback.
Now distinguished.

That's the second time in this batch a test written to *demonstrate*
quality instead *found* a defect.

## Gates

fmt · clippy `-D warnings` · 48 test groups with **byte-parity green and
unchanged** · `./compiler/go` exit 0, zero failures, **print-rust
10/10** · version gates checked with CI's own regexes at 0.31.115.
